prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent osquery/osquery release stream from 5.0.0 through 5.23.0, covering major feature introductions like Apple Silicon support, Windows on Arm, new tables, security updates, and deprecations.

chunks.memory_unit_text: In the osquery/osquery release 5.0.0, the project publishes an initial draft of the 5.0 release, noting that this release may be deleted.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.0.1, osquery 5.0 is announced as a tremendously exciting release. Installation now uses /opt/osquery on macOS and Linux for better portability. The default macOS installation uses an application bundle to support entitlement-based features. Endpoint Security APIs are used for various event-based tables on macOS. An osquery-organization macOS code signing certificate is now used. Breaking changes include installation path changes from /usr/local to /opt/osquery, macOS codesigning now done through the Osquery Foundation account, the need to update macOS full disk permission profiles, removal of the deprecated blacklist key from configuration, and changed search semantics on the augeas table. Table changes include adding secureboot for Linux and Windows, tpm_info for Windows, fixing osquery_info build_platform on Linux, supporting pid_with_namespace in more tables, updating augeas to use native pattern matching (breaking), updating chrome_extensions to include Edge and EdgeBeta, updating disk_encryption to support QueryContext, updating last to include utmp type name column, updating sudoers to support newer include syntax, and updating user_ssh_keys to detect encryption of ed25519 keys. Under the hood improvements include adding ruby namespace to thrift definition, always initializing variable change in PerformanceChange, removing deprecated blacklist key, using total_size within watchdog on Windows, supporting AF_PACKET sockets reporting on Linux, and socket_events improvements in Linux audit system. Bug fixes include adding case sensitive pragma to the pragma/actions authorizer allow list, adding feature to skip denylist for event-based queries, changing logger_mode flag to be correctly interpreted as octal, preventing osquery from creating multiple copies of the extension running at once, fixing Linux audit rule removal upon osquery exit, fixing broadcasting empty logs to logger plugins, fixing issues applying ACLs during chocolatey deployment, and fixing a memory issue.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.1.0, new features include allowing custom cpu limit duration for the watchdog and supporting custom endpoints for AWS Kinesis and Firehose. Table changes include adding docker_container_envs table for access to docker container environment and updating the curl table to return peer certificates even if the TLS handshake does not complete. Under the hood improvements include allowing tests and SDK to reset dispatcher state, avoiding string copies when looping through cron search dirs, and respecting read_max flag when hashing using ssdeep. Bug fixes include detecting when an extension has not started correctly on Windows, fixing crash when osquery captures kill syscall when not subscribed to them, fixing crash in AuditdNetlinkReader::configureAuditService when audit_add_rule_data returns an error, fixing crash when windows_security_products errors out, fixing cleanup of some event tables never occurring, improving BPF publisher reliability, lowering log level of executing distributed query, and reducing excessive log messages from authorized_keys table implementation. Documentation includes adding 5.0.1 CHANGELOG, fixing typos in Everything in SQL docs and SQL docs, updating GitHub issue templates, updating installation guide to use newer macOS paths, and updating macOS ESF documentation. Packs include adding Forcepoint Endpoint Chrome Extension detection and beurk rootkit detection. Build changes include allowing tests to reset the restarting state, building librpm with ndb support, customizable installation logic, fixing ASL test on macOS 11 and later, restoring query packs in Windows packaging, skipping deprecated ASL test when targeting macOS 10.13+ SDK, updating packaging commit to fix Linux symlinks, and updating the CI Linux Docker image.
In the osquery/osquery release 5.2.0, the release note directs users to use version 5.2.2 instead.
In the osquery/osquery release 5.2.1, the release note directs users to use version 5.2.2 instead.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.2.2, osquery brings native Apple Silicon (M1) support to the macOS platform. It also represents a comprehensive review and update of third-party dependencies. New features include Apple Silicon support. Deprecation notices include the cpuid table being x86 only, the smart_drive_info table being deprecated and not included in M1 builds, and the lldp_neighbors table being deprecated and not included in M1 builds. Table changes include updating the time table to always reflect UTC values, hiding the deprecated antispyware column in windows_security_center, and adding windows_firewall_rules table for Windows. Bug fixes include updating the ATC table path column check to be case insensitive, fixing a crash introduced by 5.2.0 when Yara uses its own strutils functions, and fixing user_time and system_time unit in processes table on M1. Documentation includes fixing typos and adding CHANGELOG 5.1.0. Build changes include updating sqlite to version 3.37.0, fixing linking of thirdparty_sleuthkit, fixing how tables are disabled in the fuzzer init method, preventing running discovery queries when fuzzing, adding BOOST_USE_ASAN define when enabling Asan, removing unnecessary macOS version check, fixing submodule cache for macOS CI runner, adding osquery version to macOS app bundle Info.plist, and updating various libraries: OpenSSL to 1.1.1l, augeas to 1.12.0, aws-sdk to 1.9.116, boost to 1.77, gflags to 2.2.2, glog to 0.5.0, googletest to 1.11.0, libarchive to 3.5.2, libcap to 1.2.59, libmagic to 5.40, librdkafka to 1.8.0, and more.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.2.3, osquery is a security update that focuses on updating some third-party libraries which contained CVEs that could affect osquery. Additionally, some other third-party libraries and tables have been dropped since they were not maintained or considered safe anymore. Deprecation notices include removing the shortcut_files table, removing the ssdeep library and its support in the hash table, and removing the libelfin library and elf parsing tables. Hardening includes updating OpenSSL from version 1.1.1l to 1.1.1n, updating zlib from v1.2.11 to v1.2.12, updating librpm to 4.17.0, and updating expat from version 2.2.10 to 2.4.7.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.3.0, osquery brings several table improvements and bugfixes. Deprecation notices include deprecating the unmaintainable legacy table smart_drive_info. New features include adding the option tls_disable_status_log to prevent status logs from being sent via TLS and adding SQLite function in_cidr_block to check if IPv4/v6 addresses are within the supplied CIDR block. Table changes include adding the admindir column to the deb_packages table to parse package databases on different paths, implementing and fixing wifi_networks on macOS Big Sur and newer, adding windows/darwin support to npm_packages, moving apt_sources and yum_sources tables to linux only, adding homebrew paths to the python_packages table, marking wall_time column in osquery_schedule as hidden, adding new metrics and improving description of existing ones in osquery_schedule, adding the mirrorlist column in the table yum_sources, implementing output_size for osquery_schedule, using additional instead of index for the admindir column in deb_packages table, adding Linux support to certificates table, adding translated column to processes table to indicate whether the process is running under Apple Rosetta, adding the internet password type to the macOS keychain_items table, and adding original filename column to file table on Windows. Bug fixes include fixing watchdog not killing unhealthy worker/extension fast enough, fixing the test_http_server.py --persist option, updating profile.py --leaks for python3, fixing osquery tls connections to aws kinesis when tls_server_certs is set, fixing parsing issue when a backslash is the last character on sudoers file line, changing the JSON of the results coming from an event scheduled query to an array, fixing globToRegex truncating UTF16 characters, preventing hanging when the WMI server does not respond, fixing python_packages table so that it lists python packages from any user Python installations, and setting str...

In the osquery/osquery release 5.4.0, new features include extending macOS Endpoint Security to include File Integrity monitoring with the new es_process_file_events table and adding Docker build scripts and configuration. Deprecation notices include preventing CLI_FLAGs to be set via config and removing the lldp_neighbors table. Table changes include new tables: es_process_file_events for macOS Endpoint Security based FIM, password_policy table for macOS, and windows_update_history. Other table changes include adding memory_available to linux memory_info table, porting the cpu_info table to linux, removing the lldp_neighbors table, updating deb_packages table to not display arch info in the package name, updating hardware_model in the system_info table on Apple M1 machines to report correctly, and updating shared_resources table to add type names and fix type/maximum_allowed handling. Under the hood improvements include expanding env vars before trying to enumerate crashes in windows_crashes table, implementing a split and trim function using std::string_view, improving scheduled query denylisting and scheduler shutdown, preventing CLI_FLAGs to be set via config, and removing unnecessary string copy. Bug fixes include adding linwin to list of supported PLATFORM_DIRS, fixing AWS certificate verification failing on all services, fixing MBCS support on Windows, fixing local_timezone column in the time table on Windows, fixing system_info table to support unicode on Windows, fixing multiple Yara leaks, fixing std::bad_alloc on pci_devices on Apple Silicon macs, fixing tables spec files to specify linux and not posix, and fixing thrift server shutting down when dropping privileges. Documentation includes CHANGELOG 5.3.0, excluding spec/example.table when generating documentation, fixing a UUID typo in the disk_encryption table, fixing spelling of the word owned, and fixing typo in FIM docs for Windows.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.5.1, osquery has some really exciting table updates. There is a much anticipated unified_log for macOS, which is the replacement for asl and uses the current Apple APIs. Additionally, several tables have improved their cross-platform support. New features include adding a denylist mechanism to distributed queries. Table changes include adding cgroup_path column to processes table on Linux, adding firmware_type column to platform_info table on Windows, adding unified_log table for macOS (UAL), porting memory_devices table to Windows, porting platform_info table to M1 Macs, restoring macOS kernel_panics table on modern macOS, updating battery table on macOS M1 with correct raw battery max and current capacity, updating mdfind query timeout to 30 seconds, updating macOS password_policy table to use -1 as sentinel value for uid column, updating parsing of authorized_keys file, and updating the registry table to be case insensitive for key. Under the hood improvements include adding a mechanism to reduce memory retained on Linux, adding denylist mechanism to distributed queries, adding table spec support for COLLATE NOCASE, improving Pidfile handling, preventing the audit event system from using too much memory, and using full pathnames while creating an archive in carves. Bug fixes include fixing GetMemorySize for Windows memory_devices table, fixing tpm_info bug where values were out of date, fixing a crash when parsing ATC config with no columns, and fixing bug in GetHomeDirectories filesystem function. Documentation includes adding core to the type column description of osquery_extensions schema, adding documentation about 3rd-party dependency security, adding example for hostname form in curl_certificate table, adding info on how to use GTEST_FILTER on windows, changelog 5.4.0, describing user-context-related caveat for screenlock table, updating schema for process_open_sockets.state, and updating schema to reflect platform_info columns not available in Windows.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.6.0, table changes include adding firmware_type column to platform_info on macOS, adding additional vendor support for the windows wmi_bios_info table, fixing docker_container_processes on macOS, fixing process_file_events subscriber being incorrectly initialized, fixing secureboot on windows by acquiring the necessary process privileges, improving macOS mdfind by reducing table overhead and supporting interruption, removing binary column from firefox_addons table, and removing is_running column from macOS running_apps table. Under the hood improvements include adding notes field to the schema and associated json, adding extended platforms to the schema and associated json, fixing a leak and improving users and groups APIs on Windows, having --tls_dump output body to stderr, improvements to osquery AWS logic, and removing leftover FreeBSD related code and documentation. Documentation includes CHANGELOG 5.5.1, correcting the description on how to configure and use Yara signature urls, documenting difference between yara and yara_events, linking to the slack archives, and updating docs that _changes tables are not evented. Build changes include deleting temporary CTest files, fixing table tests for macOS running_apps, fixing table tests for windows platform_info, migrating jobs from ubuntu-18.04 to ubuntu-20.04, and removing unused find_packages modules and submodule.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.7.0, CVEs addressed by updating a library include ignoring libzstd CVE-2021-24031. New features include a new table security_profile_info to retrieve security profile information on Windows. Table changes include adding column to es_process_events for process codesigning flags, shimcache only checking CurrentControlSet to avoid duplicate rows, processes fixing the procfs memory unit kB which is 1024 bytes not 1000, fixing permissions on opening pipes for reading in pipes table, fixing the empty host column from logged_in_users table, docker_containers not reporting finished_at for a container which is still running, and processes stabilizing the start_time column value on macOS and Linux. Bug fixes include not accessing the AWS SDK request content type if missing, fixing deadlock when logging happens during a database reset, and fixing handling of some errors during an AWS HTTP request. Documentation includes CHANGELOG 5.6.0, adding link to official YARA docs, and fixing typo in keychain_items. Packs include incident_response: process_memory_map is also applicable to Darwin. Build changes include cve: ignore zstd CVE-2021-24031, ci: add a job and helper scripts to periodically scan for CVEs, ci: update how we set github workflow step outputs, and ci: fix python version when installing modules and testing on macos.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.8.1, new features include recording and sending statistics for distributed queries. Table changes include adding ETW-based process events table for Windows, adding pid_with_namespace for yara table, adding a new table kernel_keys to the Linux platform, leaving min_version empty in xprotect_meta when not specified, porting the secureboot table to macOS, updating docker_container_stats table to include cached_memory column, porting cpu_info table to macOS x86 and Apple Silicon, implementing a new bpf_process_events_v2 table as an experiment, and adding new unit_file_state column to systemd_units. Under the hood improvements include setting counter consistently so zero always indicates all records, supporting logging empty result set in batch format for initial runs, supporting rollbacks of osquery when new versions introduce new column families, adding --pack flag to analysis.py to load queries from a pack file, and logging number of queries loaded and raising an error if 0 are loaded in profile.py. Bug fixes include clearing cached constraints and columns in xBestIndex, fixing assert fail for unverified WMI request result, fixing leaks in scheduled_tasks, flushing console buffer during ungraceful exit, propagating windows errors to the exit code, relaxing osquery safe permissions check, silencing warnings for more builtin Chrome and Brave extensions, workaround for hung routes table, fixing typo in dns_resolvers when spawning in namespace, and fixing flaky test_daemon_sigint. Documentation includes adding note about windows_security_products compatibility, CHANGELOG 5.7.0, mentioning the recent adoption of automatic CVE scanning, fixing broken link in CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, updating the list of pages, and clarifying that logger_plugin is set from CLI. Build changes include not catching table or registry exceptions when running tests, and more.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.8.2, this is a hotfix for how osquery's COM security initialization works. Bug fixes include fixing empty batch result set reporting, fixing COM security initialization by setting COM security per interface level, and fixing username field in managed_policy table. Documentation includes CHANGELOG 5.8.1. Build changes include test: do not always expect a row from the secureboot table, cmake: only link against the experiments loader when needed, tests: fix some tests becoming osquery shells, test: fix SystemdUnitsTest missing the unit_file_state column, and tests: do not always build root tests on Linux.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.9.1, a big shoutout for the Windows Arm port. New features include adding support for Windows on Arm and adding new string_batch request type to compliment existing string type in logger. Table changes include adding connected_displays table on macOS, adding windows_search table, restoring functionality of crashes table on macOS 12 and newer, updating keychain_items to include data about key types, updating os_version to include Apple RSR fields using native API, updating safari_extensions to handle the current app extensions pattern, updating system_info to include the number of sockets, and updating unified_log table to add predicate column and optimize timestamp constraint. Under the hood improvements include improving listDirectoriesInDirectory by using std::fs, not considering a 404 as an error in ec2-instance-metadata, releasing objects and freeing memory obtained from COM, not passing wstring::c_str() to wstringToString function, and not copying process arguments into vector for CreateProcess call. Bug fixes include fixing version column in homebrew_packages, improving extended_attributes implementation for Linux and macOS, and updating event tables to mark time column as additional. Documentation includes updating expired Slack invite, updating es_process_file_events.table description, and CHANGELOG 5.8.2. Build changes include cve: update to openssl 1.1.1u, cmake: add an option to disable shallow git clone operations, fixing the aarch64 workflow, test: fix a leak in ExtendedAttributesTableTests SetUp function, cve: update libxml2 to v2.11.2, libs: bring out LZ4 from rdkafka and update it to v1.9.4, ci: update python version and docs build tools, ci: update aarch64 runner to Ubuntu 20.04 and update badges, and add few unit tests for the hashing component.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.10.2, this release has several updates and bugfixes. One potential breaking change is in how the watchdog calculates CPU utilization, now based on virtual cores instead of physical CPUs. A second potential breaking change is in PR #8102, which allows decorations to the top level of the status logs and normalizes the decorations format to the results log, meaning that unixTime, severity and line JSON fields are now numbers instead of strings. New features include adding --enable_watchdog_debug flag and improving watchdog error messages, adding --aws_enforce_fips to enforce AWS FIPS endpoints, adding new AWS valid regions, and implementing decorations_top_level flag for status logs. Table changes include adding new macOS SIP config flags, adding cloud_id to ycloud_instance_metadata, allowing querying of kernel and filesystem drivers, updating es_process_file_events adding support for open events and for only triggering on file_paths, updating firefox_addons to use rapidjson to parse and don't block on read, updating macOS es_process_events table to quote spaces in command line and environment variables, updating linux disk_encryption to recursively query parent crypt status, and adding and reverting indexing on block_devices. Under the hood improvements include adding warnings when an enrollment secret cannot be found, avoiding blocking when reading plist files, fixing named virtual table create statement, removing forensicReadFile, substituting the TEXT macro with SQL_TEXT in table code, using JSON member iterator instead of rescanning, avoiding checking if a file exists before opening, avoiding unnecessary string conversions, and using virtual cores to calculate CPU utilization limit in watchdog. Bug fixes include always locking event_index_mutex when accessing event_index map, checking audit return values with <=, fixing wifi_survey table not to crash if the ssid cannot be retrieved, and fixing macOS...

In the osquery/osquery release 5.11.0, table changes include adding new table vscode_extensions, adding support for additional Apple Silicon columns in secureboot table, adding Shortcut metadata parsing on Windows in the file table, removing atom_packages table, and adding additional chrome extensions paths to pick up extensions for Chrome Beta, Chrome Dev, and Vivaldi. Under the hood improvements include adding version collations to column definitions, adding support for additional collations in column definitions, adding version collate functions, adding cache and throttling for certificates, keychain_acls, and keychain_items tables to reduce the occurrence of keychain corruption due to broken macOS APIs, and marking pid column as additional instead of index in process_open_sockets. Bug fixes include adding stricter checks to JSON parsing, fixing signed/unsigned mismatch in powershell_events, fixing a crash in firefox_addons, and correcting the aws_sts_region behavior. Documentation includes updating building.md prereqs for Windows, correcting link to a PR in the 4.7.0 changelog, calling out in the CHANGELOG the format changes of the status logs decorations, removing some duplicated lines from 5.8.1 changelog, fixing typo in table specs, keychain cache and throttling documentation, and changelog 5.10.2. Build / Dependencies include updating libxml2 to v2.12.3, updating zlib to 1.3 and ignoring a CVE, updating openssl to 3.2.0, updating nvdlib to use the latest NVD APIs, fixing Linux build, correcting job order, re-enabling tools_tests_testrelease, enabling client certificate verification in the TLS tests, and temporary workaround to build with XCode 15.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.12.1, new features include a new flag logger_tls_backoff_max to configure the retry backoff for TLS logger plugin. Table changes include porting the battery table to Windows, updating homebrew_packages table to include Casks, updating cpu_info to include load_percentage on windows, checking path exists first in vscode_extensions, deb_packages to ignore non existent admindirs, adding missing path separator in Safari Extensions table generator, and adding windows UBR to os_version table. Under the hood improvements include persisting query performance stats, deprecating worker_threads flag, changing message from warning to error when extension could not be loaded, refactoring macOS system profile report retrieval, and clearing performance stats when modifying scheduled/pack query. Bug fixes include fixing version collate returning incorrect value when last character is a delimiter, fixing a memory leak in unified_log, and not adding ATC table name to registry until after sqlite DB initialization. Documentation includes updating Jinja dependency for docs, removing Zercurity from fleet managers list, fixing missing spaces in kernel_keys column descriptions, and updating description for amperage in battery table. Packs include fixing packs to check for platform before including queries. Build changes include downgrading sqlite to 3.42 to prevent a regression with required columns, cve: remove libxml2 dependency, cve: update libexpat to 2.6.0, cve: update sqlite to 3.45.0, cve: update openssl to 3.2.1, ci: use all available cores and print more stats, cmake: pass the osquery python path to googletest, test: fix vscodeExtensions.test_sanity test, and cmake: correct typo semvar -> semver.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.12.2, this release is a hot fix. It reverts #8233, which had inadvertently broken ATC tables under some conditions. Bug fixes include reverting 'Don't add ATC table name to registry until after sqlite DB initialization #8233'. Build changes include CI: fix macOS python dependencies install step.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.13.1, a Windows codesigning note mentions that the Windows binaries and MSI package have been signed with the Fleet Device Management codesigning certificate as the osquery project is currently working on identity verification to get a new signing certificate. Table changes include the Python manifest directories .egg-info and .dist-info containing flat file hierarchies, users table on linux by default returning only users in /etc/passwd, adding sha256 hash to apparmor_profiles table, adding support for metalink and storing repo config file name in yum_sources table, updating user_ssh_keys with additional details for OpenSSL-style keys, fixing dns_resolvers dns-search bug with multiple search domains, fixing process_open_sockets to correctly display family and protocol on macOS, and adding missing SSH key types to authorized_keys that support FIDO2 authentication. Under the hood improvements include improving error message when required constraint missing and adding verbose logging when distributed requests fail and retry. Bug fixes include fixing crash in rpm_packages table by upgrading librpm from 4.18.0 to 4.18.2, fixing crash in linux file monitoring related to NFS mounted directories, fixing listDirectoriesInDirectory to check if symlinks point to directories (fixes inotify warnings flooded in logs), fixing potential memory leak in class ServiceArgumentParser's Constructor, fixing crash in ServiceArgumentParser via ServiceMain, fixing real precision by limiting precision to 15 digits, fixing invalid memory access in curl_certificates table, adding pending state to ATC tables to avoid duplicate sql attaches and reverting ATC changes from #8233 that caused a race condition and ATC table failure, and fixing crash when carve size is stored as string. Documentation includes updating Time Machine table documentation to require FDA, updating processes table spec and docs to remove outdated column alias, filling in missing column descriptions to spec for device_partitions, improving explanation of required columns, updating package_receipts table example, and removing some duplicated words from code comments and strings.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.14.1, starting with Osquery 5.14, the codesigning has changed; henceforth releases will be signed by an osquery specific signing key issued by Microsoft Azure. New features include adding --yara_sigurl_authenticate flag. Table changes include adding additional WMI data to deviceguard_status table, fixing linux groups table to handle larger group sets by increasing buffer size, adding support for Firefox addons for snap installations, removing support for deprecated Safari Legacy Extensions, macOS 15 alf support, updating table alf_explicit_auths as not supported on macOS 15, updating table alf_exceptions to support macOS 15, fixing windows_crashes missing information on user mode memory dumps, fixing safari_extensions not returning results, and renaming hvci_status to deviceguard_status to better reflect the data collected. Under the hood improvements include adding column optimization support to allow processing IN constraints all at once in xFilter, minor improvements to the hashing logic, and refactoring readFile. Bug fixes include fixing unified_log handling of timestamp formats, fixing crash with non-null-terminated values in registry enumeration, fixing check and free cert context creation in windows certificates table, fixing handle strftime potential error in the time table, and fixing crash in socket table parsing on windows. Build changes include running tests on macos-15, updating tests for unified_log table to work around slowness, ensuring python http server is ready to serve, extending timeout for test HTTP server, upgrading GitHub Actions upload-artifact to v4, Boost 1.86 compatibility, cleanups and fixes for a newer clang toolchain, updating the upload-artifact action to v4.4.0, silencing deprecation warnings about non standard extensions on VS2022, adding missing includes causing compilation error with Clang 18.1.8, and bumping actions/download-artifact from 2 to 4.1.7.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.15.0, table changes include adding arc path to chrome_extensions on macOS, using empty columns instead of zeroes when undefined in socket_events, adding support for accept to macOS table socket_events, adding all-platform user-based optimized columns, adding columns to es_process_events, adding Darwin platform optimized miscellaneous columns, adding all-platform path-based optimized columns, adding Windows platform optimized columns, adding hash_executable column to signature table, including VSCode Insiders extensions in vscode_extensions table, adding POSIX platforms optimized columns, adding Linux platform optimized columns, adding all platform process based and curl optimized columns, adding Darwin platform optimized system-related columns, adding Darwin platform optimized path columns, fixing incorrect SID in logged_in_users table on windows when username and domain/device name are the same, updating the browser_firefox table to exclude Crash Reports and Pending Pings folders, and moving status column to extended_schema for linux socket_events. Under the hood improvements include optimizing default status message constructor in Utils. Bug fixes include fixing a leak in genAarch64PlatformInfo, fixing a leak in DiskArbitrationEventPublisher::getProperty, catching generic exception in order to avoid crashing when parsing windows events logs, fixing leak in windows_events by using scope_guard, fixing eBPF's parsing of parent pid, and fixing IO objects refcounting. Documentation includes adding documentation for testing macOS EndpointSecurity, adding double quotes in Windows installation documentation, updating expired Slack invite, and updating docs to correctly define conditional_to_base64. Build changes include bumping jinja2 from 3.1.4 to 3.1.5, removing yara schema subdirectory, adding chrono header file, and replacing usage...

In the osquery/osquery release 5.16.0, table changes include fixing the python_paths table to skip unnecessary code paths when filtering by directory, adding python packages in user directories on python_packages, adding RHEL paths for python_packages table, buffering error logs in deb_packages table, fixing wifi_status to correctly gather network_name on MacOS 14+, fixing hardware model and version on Lenovo on system_info, and optimizing rpm_packages and rpm_package_files use of query context. Bug fixes include fixing to only deny-list scheduled queries when watchdog is enabled and switching to wmain to accept non-ascii characters from command line.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.17.0, changes include adding CHANGELOG.md entry for 5.16.0, adding symlink_target_path to files tables, ignoring libarchive CVE-2024-26256, fixes in windows helpers, aligning ES functions with documented macOS versions, fixing include path in logger-plugins.md, fixing integration test name in Windows build instructions, fixing event expiration to prevent losing events, updating shell_history table to include ash, fixing docker container table disk/write metrics by comparing op values with ignore case, escaping service binary path in manage-osqueryd.ps1, updating docker_container_stats table to include memory_inactive_file and memory_total_inactive_file, adding auto_update and app_name column to homebrew_packages table, adding support for scheduled queries to run at startup, Boost 1.87 compatibility, pinning macos python versions in CI to fix mismatch between builder and test runner, ignoring util-linux CVE-2024-28085, bumping jinja2 from 3.1.5 to 3.1.6, fixing SMC reading values, fixing network metrics, implementing yara_events table for Windows, fixing flaky mdfind test in CI, updating openssl from 3.2.1 to 3.4.1, adding support for DEB822-style apt sources, adding support for msix packages, implementing dns_lookup_events table on Windows, adding UpgradeCode to programs table, bumping expat from 2.6.0 to 2.7.1, updating ubuntu runners to 22.04, refactoring ETW helpers for unicode support, fixing startup items parsing, and filtering the Win32_Processor query to only required fields.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.18.1, changes include printing stderr if exists in performance analysis, updating googletest, fixing parsing of Windows shortcut (.lnk) files in file table, fixing Prefetch table for Windows 11, updating libarchive from 3.6.2 to 3.7.9, fixing hardware UUID caching, adding detection for ARM CPUs when running in x86 emulation, reducing log noise for hash table, fixing SQL example syntax in SQL introduction docs, adding jetbrains_plugins table, and adding recent_files table on Windows.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.19.0, features include adding table deb_package_files, adding system_profiler table for macOS, adding version collate to os_version table's version column, adding entitlements column to macOS signature table, and adding support for VSCode forks in vscode_extensions. Bugfixes include fixing NSInvalidArgumentException when querying connected_displays, fixing inconsistent counter resets due to Config::purge(), updating linux block_device and disk_encryption source data to simple sysfs implementation, and fixing ATC for open Firefox databases. Other changes include updating yara from 4.2.3 to 4.5.4, upgrading zlib to 1.3.1, fixing build for XCode SDK 16.4, updating build instructions for workaround for XCode SDK > 16.3, adding Cursor AI editor configurations, further improvement to Cursor rules, and updating Windows build instructions.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.20.0, features/bugs include adding default path for CA certificate bundle on openSUSE, excluding config views from db migration, making vscode_extensions more consistently report UUID, not overwriting hardware_version if it has a value, supporting nvm on npm_packages table, and adding scoped npm package support in npm_packages table. Dependencies include fixing build against libaudit >=4.1.1 by removing set_aumessage_mode call and updating libarchive from 3.7.9 to 3.8.1. Documentation includes fixing SQL examples for system_profiler table, adding more informative descriptions for mounts.blocks_free and mounts.blocks_available, and updating dns_resolvers documentation to point to interface_details on Windows.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.21.0, changes include improvements to password_policy table, improving file traversal performance and correctness, adding support for Login Items and Background Services on modern macOS, adding last_connected_automatic and last_connected_manual to wifi_networks table, refreshing resolver state on interval to pick up DNS changes, adding new darwin certificate trust settings table, fixing crash when querying carves table with carves larger than 2GB, and adding support for gzip content-encoding in HTTP client.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.22.1, 5.22.0 macOS binaries will not execute because the signing certificate is out of sync with the provisioning profile; 5.22.1 replaces it. Features include making escapeNonPrintableBytes UTF-8 aware (which changes some query results that formerly were rendered as raw unicode bytes and will now be rendered as the corresponding characters), updating virtual sql functions to support multiple constraints (allowing queries that join or subquery to the users table to include results for remote users), adding support for retries in carver, preserving file metadata in carver archives, and adding machine-wide provisioned MSIX packages to programs table. Build & Dependencies include updating osquery-toolchain to 1.2.0 (LLVM 11.0.0, zlib 1.2.13), updating Apple provisioning profile for new developer certificates, suppressing enum-constexpr-conversion error for boost mpl on macos, and updating openssl to 3.6.1. Fixes include quitting carving when sending a block fails, fixing SMBIOS CPU count, fixing systemd unit to use .target instead of .service, fixing typo in winbaseobj.table description, fixing JSON handling copy vs. ref semantics, and fixing memory leak in logon_sessions.

In the osquery/osquery release 5.23.0, features include adding process memory scanning capability to yara table, splitting yara tables into yara_process and yara_file, adding Windows process_open_handles table, adding secureboot_certificates table for Linux, extending python_packages and npm_packages to cover modern package managers, adding level filtering to the unified_log table, disallowing newlines in curl custom headers, supplementing LaunchServices with directory scanning in apps table, adding command line flags for query input and output, adding new header-based authentication mechanism for remote APIs, adding recursion to npm_packages, making profile.py performance thresholds configurable via CLI flags, and adding ROOT\default to WMI tables. Build & Dependencies include updating expat to 2.7.4 to fix CVE-2026-25210 and fixing GCC 15 compatibility. Fixes include fixing macOS keychain corruption when accessing non-SSV keychain files by copying to temporary files first, fixing incorrect example queries in table specs, improving network_name detection on macOS wifi_status table, fixing a bug in apt_sources parsing, adding NOCASE and VERSION collation to various columns, increasing the limit on systemd unit iteration, fixing format string vulnerability in shell.cpp disconnect_socket(), fixing saving file times in file carves, fixing empty results from office_mru table, fixing multiple security vulnerabilities in smc_keys.cpp, fixing gatekeeper table on macOS 15+, fixing container bounds checking vulnerabilities, and reducing noisy logs from chrome_extensions.

In the pallets/flask release 2.0.0, the project announces new major versions of all core Pallets libraries including Flask 2.0, with a significant amount of work and many changes, and advises careful reading of the changelog and using tools like pip-compile and Dependabot to pin dependencies.
In the pallets/flask release 2.0.1, the project provides a link to the changes for version 2.0.1.
In the pallets/flask release 2.0.2, the project provides a link to the changes for version 2.0.2.
In the pallets/flask release 2.0.3, the project provides a link to the changes and a milestone link for version 2.0.3.

In the pallets/flask release 2.1.0, the project announces a feature release that includes new features and removes previously deprecated features, makes the 2.1.x branch the supported bugfix branch, and encourages upgrading along with other Pallets projects like Werkzeug 2.1, Jinja 3.1, Click 8.1, MarkupSafe 2.1, and ItsDangerous 2.1.
In the pallets/flask release 2.1.1, the project provides a fix release for the 2.1.0 feature release, with a link to changes and a milestone.
In the pallets/flask release 2.1.2, the project provides a fix release for the 2.1.0 feature release, with a link to changes and a milestone.
In the pallets/flask release 2.1.3, the project provides a link to changes and a milestone for version 2.1.3.

In the pallets/flask release 2.2.0, the project announces a feature release that includes new features and removes previously deprecated code, makes the 2.2.x branch the supported bug fix branch, and encourages upgrading and using pip-tools to pin dependencies.
In the pallets/flask release 2.2.1, the project provides a fix release for the 2.2.0 feature release, with a link to changes and a milestone.
In the pallets/flask release 2.2.2, the project provides a fix release for the 2.2.0 feature release, with a link to changes and a milestone.
In the pallets/flask release 2.2.3, the project provides a fix release for the 2.2.x release branch, with a link to changes and a milestone.
In the pallets/flask release 2.2.4, the project provides a fix release for the 2.2.x release branch, with a link to changes and a milestone.

In the pallets/flask release 2.3.0, the project announces a feature release that includes new features, removes previously deprecated code, adds new deprecations, makes the 2.3.x branch the supported fix branch, and encourages upgrading and testing with warnings treated as errors.
In the pallets/flask release 2.3.1, the project provides a fix release for the 2.3.x release branch, with a link to changes and a milestone.
In the pallets/flask release 2.3.2, the project provides a security fix release for the 2.3.x release branch, referencing security advisory GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq and CVE-2023-30861.

In the pallets/flask release 2.2.5, the project provides a security fix release for the 2.2.x release branch, referencing security advisory GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq and CVE-2023-30861, and notes that 2.3.x is the currently supported release branch.
In the pallets/flask release 2.3.3, the project provides a fix release for the 2.3.x feature branch, with a link to changes and a milestone.

In the pallets/flask release 3.0.0, the project announces a feature release that includes new features, removes previously deprecated code, adds new deprecations, makes the 3.0.x branch the supported fix branch, and encourages upgrading and testing with warnings treated as errors.

In the pallets/flask release 3.0.1, the project provides a fix release for the 3.0.x feature release branch, fixing an issue where using other JSON providers such as flask-orjson previously caused loaded session data to have an incorrect format in some cases.
In the pallets/flask release 3.0.2, the project provides a fix release for the 3.0.x feature release branch, fixing bugs but not otherwise changing behavior and should not result in breaking changes.

In the pallets/flask release 3.0.3, the project provides a fix release for the 3.0.x feature branch, with fixes including not accessing hashlib.sha1 at import time for FIPS builds and not initializing the cli attribute in the sansio scaffold.

In the pallets/flask release 3.1.0, the project announces a feature release that may include new features, removes previously deprecated code, adds new deprecations, or introduces potentially breaking changes. It drops support for Python 3.8, updates minimum dependency versions to Werkzeug >= 3.1, ItsDangerous >= 2.2, Blinker >= 1.9, provides a configuration option to control automatic option responses, adds encoding parameter to open_resource methods, allows per-request customization of max_content_length, adds support for Partitioned cookie attribute, supports key rotation with SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS, fixes host_matching and subdomain_matching interaction with SERVER_NAME, and checks Request.trusted_hosts during routing.

In the pallets/flask release 3.1.1, the project provides a fix release that fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior. It fixes signing key selection order when key rotation is enabled via SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS (GHSA-4grg-w6v8-c28g), fixes type hint for cli_runner.invoke, ensures flask --help loads the app and plugins first, and marks sans-io base class as being able to handle views that return AsyncIterable.

In the pallets/flask release 3.1.2, the project provides a fix release that fixes bugs but does not otherwise change behavior. It fixes stream_with_context inside async views, ensures the final state of session is correct when using follow_redirects in the test client, and relaxes type hint for passing bytes IO to send_file.

In the pallets/flask release 3.1.3, the project provides a security fix release that fixes a security issue but does not otherwise change behavior. It marks the session as accessed for operations that only access the keys but not the values, such as in and len, referencing GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726.

prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent pbatard/rufus release stream from v3.8 through v4.14, covering bug fixes, new features, and platform support changes.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.8 [BUGFIX RELEASE]
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.8, the project fixes a regression where some ISOs (e.g. Debian) would produce a Syslinux error when booted in BIOS mode, and fixes a potential 0xC0030057 error when trying to create persistent partitions on a non-FIXED drive on Windows 10 1703 or earlier.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.9
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.9, the project adds experimental exFAT support when creating blank UEFI:NTFS drives, fixes ext2/ext3 corruption for partitions larger than 4 GB, fixes early boot files not being usable on compressed NTFS partitions, fixes writing of compressed streams that don't end on sector boundary, fixes percent not being displayed on slow format, improves file preallocation and speeds up ISO extraction, improves ext2/ext3 formatting speed, improves protective MBR message for GPT partitioned drives, improves reporting of Syslinux/GRUB download errors, improves reporting of partition types and of Windows' version, reports the usage of UDF symbolic links, and updates embedded Syslinux to 6.04-pre1.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.10
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.10, the project improves support for Ubuntu 20.04, improves detection of FIXED drives with no mounted partitions, improves extfs formatting, updates UEFI:NTFS file system drivers to v1.5, fixes progress not being updated when using the German localization, fixes primary GPT being overwritten when adding the protective MBR message, fixes a regression with security solutions that prevent the creation of an autorun.inf, fixes an assert during FreeDOS drive creation when the Windows system locale is set to UTF-8, and fixes invalid label errors when using a non-Western locale.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.11
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.11, the project adds Rock Ridge deep directory support, adds an option to write small ISOs to an ESP (GPT only), adds a cheat mode (Ctrl-SELECT) to extract content from an additional zip archive on top of the ISO, adds a cheat mode (Alt-G) to disable Virtual Hard Disk listing, adds a cheat mode (Alt-P) to toggle a GPT ESP to Basic Data (Windows 10 only), fixes improper x86 32-bit NTFS driver being used for UEFI:NTFS, improves UEFI:NTFS compatibility with older UEFI firmwares, improves startup time by running the ISO download feature check in the background, removes Ubuntu's splash screen for persistent UEFI drives, and enables ASLR for the Rufus executable.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.12
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.12, the project adds optional SHA-512 digest algorithm (Alt-H), adds a cheat mode (Alt-+/-) to increase/decrease application priority, enables direct provision of install.wim/install.esd for Windows To Go, moves Windows To Go ESP to the beginning of the drive on systems that allow it, enforces a minimum volume size of 256 MB for ext2/ext3 partitions, speeds up the scanning of ISOs with lots of Rock Ridge deep directory entries, fixes detection of GRUB version and updates embedded GRUB for Ubuntu 20.10 support, fixes user interface labels for accessibility, and works around a Windows bug where the wrong drive letter may be returned.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.13
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.13, the project adds a cheat mode (Alt-M) to accept disk images without a Boot Marker, adds marquee operation progress to the taskbar icon, adds zeroing/image writing progress to the log, switches to using 0x55 and 0xAA instead of 0x00 and 0xFF for low pass badblock check, switches to using fake/manufacturer units when computing the default label, fixes overnumerous write retries on error when writing a disk image, works around Windows' abysmal handling of removable drives that contain an ESP, improves mounting/unmounting of volumes, updates UEFI:NTFS file system drivers to version 1.7, and includes other internal fixes and improvements (VDS, error reporting, etc.).

chunks.title: Rufus 3.14
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.14, the project improves DD write speed (uncompressed images only), improves checksum computation speed, improves network connectivity detection, only prompts for additional GRUB/Syslinux downloads when not writing in DD mode, fixes potential loss of disk after writing Ubuntu 20.10 in DD mode, fixes GRUB compatibility issue with Ubuntu 21.04, fixes Rufus MBR not being selected by default for Windows ISOs, fixes drag and drop being enabled during drive creation, and adds more exceptions for forced DD image writing.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.15
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.15, the project updates GRUB to version 2.06, adds support for .vtsi files (Ventoy Sparse Image), adds workaround for openSUSE Live ISOs, moves default app directory to %LocalAppData%\Rufus\ and always saves a log there on exit, fixes AppStore version of Rufus not being able to store downloaded files, fixes failure to open Syslinux/GRUB files when Rufus is located at the root of a drive, prevents the creation of System Volume Information on ESPs written in DD mode, prevents drive letter assignation to the UEFI:NTFS partition, prevents persistent partition creation errors due to size, enhances safety checks before running the Fido ISO download script, and includes other internal fixes and improvements.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.16
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.16, the project fixes ISO mode support for Red Hat 8.2+ and derivatives, fixes BIOS boot support for Arch derivatives, fixes removal of some boot entries for Ubuntu derivatives, fixes log not being saved on exit, adds Windows 11 Extended installation support (disables TPM/Secure Boot/RAM requirements), adds UEFI Shell ISO downloads (retroactively applied through FIDO), adds support for Intel NUC card readers, improves Windows 11 support, improves Windows version reporting, and speeds up clearing of MBR/GPT.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.17 [BUGFIX RELEASE]
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.17, the project fixes MBR not being properly cleared, fixes commandline hogger not being deleted on exit, improves ReFS handling for platforms that support it, updates UEFI:NTFS to latest and removes Secure Boot notice since this version is Secure Boot signed, and updates Grub4DOS to latest.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.18
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.18, the project fixes DLL sideloading vulnerabilities, fixes ISO to ESP creation when running on Windows 11, fixes an issue when detecting network connectivity when the DHCP service is disabled, updates FreeDOS to version 1.3, adds bypass of Windows 11 restrictions for in-place upgrades, adds Miracle Linux 8 to the list of Red Hat exceptions, and includes other internal fixes and improvements.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.19
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.19, the project adds a new selection dialog for Windows 11 setup customization, which moves Secure Boot and TPM bypass to this dialog, also allows bypassing the mandatory requirement for a Microsoft account with Windows 11 22H2 (network must be temporarily disabled or unplugged for local account creation to be proposed), also adds an option to skip all collection questions (sets all answers to "Don't allow"), also adds an option for setting internal drives offline with Windows To Go (these customization options are only proposed when using a Windows 11 image), adds support for distros using a nonstandard GRUB 2.0 prefix directory (openSUSE Live, GeckoLinux), adds the ability to ignore USBs, changes drive listing to always list in increasing order of size, updates exceptions needed by Red Hat and derivatives for the 9.x releases, updates UEFI:NTFS drivers to latest, reassigns a letter for drives written in DD mode that don't have an ESP (e.g. CoreELEC), fixes Windows refusing to mount Linux MBR partitions on FIXED drives, and fixes support for multiextent files when Joliet is in use.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.20
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.20, the project enables applicable Windows User Experience options for Windows 10, remembers last Windows User Experience selection between sessions, adds automatic local account creation and regional options duplication (limited to creating an account with the same name as the current user and with an empty password that the user will be prompted to change after first reboot), adds a workaround for ISOs that have a syslinux symbolic link to /isolinux/ (Knoppix), reverts to offline insertion of registry keys for the TPM/SB/RAM bypass where possible, removes storage bypass since this is a bogus bypass that doesn't do anything, improves BIOS compatibility when displaying the "UEFI boot only" alert message, fixes Windows User Experience dialog appearing twice for Windows To Go, fixes Windows User Experience options not being applied for ARM64, fixes Microsoft Account bypass not being applied unless TPM/SB/RAM bypass is selected, and fixes overeager detection of GRUB2 bootloaders with nonstandard prefixes.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.21
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.21, the project allows the provision of an arbitrary local account username in the Windows User Experience dialog, improves Windows version reporting from ISO/.wim, updates UEFI:NTFS' NTFS drivers to v1.4 and exFAT drivers to v1.9, switches to remote download for nonstandard GRUB (Fedora 37, openSUSE Live, GeckoLinux), fixes UEFI:NTFS partition not being set in MBR mode for ISOs with a >4GB file (UwUntu), fixes GRUB support for Arch and derivatives when a non FAT compliant label is used, fixes incorrect detection of GRUB with nonstandard prefixes, and fixes tab order not working on the Windows User Experience dialog.

chunks.title: Rufus 3.22
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v3.22, the project adds SHA-1 and SHA-256 x86 acceleration on CPUs that support it, adds an option to disable BitLocker device encryption in the Windows User Experience dialog, adds a cheat mode (Ctrl-P) to preserve the log between sessions, fixes potential media creation errors by forcing the unmount of stale .wim images, fixes potential access errors in ISO to ESP mode by forcing Large FAT32 formatting, fixes user-specified label not being preserved on error/cancel, fixes some large SSD devices being listed by default, fixes processing of Rock Ridge CE fields, works around the use of Rock Ridge symbolic links for Linux firmware packages (Debian), removes the ISO download feature on Windows 7, and notes that this is the last version of Rufus that can run on Windows 7.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.0, the project fixes persistent partition not working with Ubuntu 23.04, fixes out of range pointer error with Ubuntu 23.04 when booting in BIOS mode, fixes boot freeze with Ubuntu Studio when Secure Boot is enabled, fixes incorrect architecture detection when checking for updates, fixes a Windows Store application crash when processing GRUB bootloaders, fixes a Windows Store application crash when enumerating processes that contain a % sign, fixes a Windows Store application crash when using German localization, and notes that the major version was bumped because new versions of Rufus require Windows 8 or later, default to a 64-bit executable, and old versions potentially not being able to update properly.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.1, the project adds timeouts on enumeration queries that may stall on some systems, restores MS-DOS drive creation through the download of binaries from Microsoft, updates the log button icon, fixes UEFI:NTFS incompatibility with Windows Dev Kit 2023 platform, and fixes more GRUB out of range pointer errors with Ubuntu/Fedora when booting in BIOS mode.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.2
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.2, the project adds detection and warning for UEFI revoked bootloaders (including ones revoked through SkuSiPolicy.p7b), adds ZIP64 support to extract .zip images that are larger than 4 GB, adds saving and restoring current drive to/from compressed VHDX image, adds saving and restoring current drive to/from compressed FFU (Full Flash Update) image [EXPERIMENTAL], fixes a crash when trying to open Windows ISOs with the MinGW compiled x86 32-bit version, fixes an issue where ISOs that contain a boot image with an EFI label are not detected as bootable, increases the ISO to ESP limit for Debian 12 netinst images, and ensures that the main partition size is aligned to the cluster size.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.3
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.3, the project adds support for symbolic link preservation when NTFS is used, adds an exception to enforce NTFS for Linux Mint's LMDE, adds an expert feature to restrict a Windows installation to S Mode, fixes persistence support for Debian 12 in BIOS mode, fixes a regression that prevented the opening of .vhd images, updates UEFI:NTFS to report a more explicit error on bootmgr security issues, improves the search for conflicting processes by running it in a background thread, and improves support for Slax Linux.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.4
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.4, the project adds workaround for distros that use broken symbolic links as their UEFI bootloaders (such as Mint 21.3), adds support for GRUB 2.12, fixes a crash when saving .ffu images, fixes UEFI:NTFS partition not being added in MBR mode for some Linux ISOs, prevents Microsoft Dev Drives from being listed, improves support for SDXC card readers, and improves Large FAT32 formatting by aligning start of data regions to 1 MB.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.5
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.5, the project adds new advanced option to perform runtime UEFI media validation of suitable images (Windows, most Linux), moves the Use Rufus MBR advanced option to a cheat mode (Alt-A), fixes truncation of VHDX images as well as a benign error message when writing VHD/VHDX, fixes support for Linux persistence in some configurations (Mint, Ubuntu 24.04), fixes multiple potential vulnerabilities, updates internal GRUB to version 2.12, updates UEFI:NTFS to latest (now always uses the ntfs-3g driver rather than the buggy AMI NTFS one), increases buffer size when copying ISO files in an attempt to minimize the AMI NTFS UEFI driver bug, improves partition creation handling, and doesn't display the WUE dialog when a conflicting unattend.xml already exists.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.6
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.6, the project adds a new setup.exe wrapper to bypass Windows 11 24H2 in-place upgrade restrictions, adds TimeZone to regional options replication, sets local account passwords to not expire by default, fixes an error when trying to write compressed VHD images, fixes an error when invoking Rufus from the PowerShell commandline, improves revoked UEFI bootloaders check to support Linux SBAT, Windows SVN and cert DBX, and improves support for ReactOS boot media.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.7
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.7, the project adds a mechanism to detect and download updated DBXs from the official UEFI repository, adds ztsd compression support for disk images, adds a new exclusion feature in the settings to ignore disks with a specific GPT GUID, improves detection for compressed VHD images that are too large to fit the target drive, fixes commandline hogger not being deleted when running Rufus from a different directory, fixes FAT filenames from embedded images being potentially truncated on image extraction, fixes a side-loading vulnerability (CVE-2025-26624) with cfgmgr32.dll, fixes UI memory leaks, falls back to user/system default locale when getting error description, doesn't run the commandline hogger on POSIX shells, drops ARM 32-bit builds (ARM 64-bit builds are NOT affected), and updates FreeDOS and Grub4DOS to latest.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.8
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.8, the project switches to wimlib for all WIM image processing, which greatly speeds up image analysis when opening Windows ISOs, can speed up Windows To Go drive creation, might help with Parallels limitations on Mac (but Rufus on Parallels is still unsupported), enables the splitting of >4GB files with Alt-E (but still way slower than using UEFI:NTFS), switches to using Visual Studio binaries everywhere due to MinGW DLL delay-loading limitations, adds more exceptions for Linux ISOs that restrict themselves to DD mode (Nobara, openSUSE, ...), improves reporting of UEFI bootloaders in the log with info on the Secure Boot status, fixes an issue with size limitations when writing an uncompressed VHD back to the same drive, fixes a crash when opening the log with the 32-bit MinGW compiled version, and fixes commandline parameters not being forwarded to original Windows setup.exe.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.9 [BUGFIX RELEASE]
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.9, the project fixes downloads from https://rufus.ie no longer working due to recent GitHub server changes, fixes unofficial Windows ISOs with single index WIMs not presenting the WUE dialog, and notes that none of the existing versions of Rufus are able to automatically detect and update to the 4.9 release, so users must upgrade manually. Also from Rufus 4.8: switches to wimlib for all WIM image processing, switches to using Visual Studio binaries everywhere, adds more exceptions for Linux ISOs that restrict themselves to DD mode, improves reporting of UEFI bootloaders in the log with info on the Secure Boot status, fixes an issue with size limitations when writing an uncompressed VHD back to the same drive, fixes a crash when opening the log with the 32-bit MinGW compiled version, and fixes commandline parameters not being forwarded to original Windows setup.exe.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.10
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.10, the project adds Dark Mode support, adds support for creating Windows CA 2023 compatible media (requires a Windows 11 25H2 ISO), adds support for saving an existing drive to ISO (UDF only), improves error reporting when saving to VHD/VHDX, improves persistence support for Linux Mint, fixes UEFI DBX updates being reported in some timezones even when there are none, fixes a situation where no file system can be selected in ISO mode, and fixes a crash when trying to process Windows ISOs with very long paths.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.11
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.11, the project adds a cheat mode (Ctrl-Alt-D) to toggle between Light and Dark mode, improves WUE option text relating to the CA 2023 option, updates Linux SBAT / Microsoft SVN Secure Boot revocation values to latest, fixes some GRUB/Syslinux download dialogs showing only the 'Close' button, fixes an assert being triggered when using the WUE CA 2023 option on its own, and fixes an application crash on systems that have a failed dynamic disk.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.12
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.12, the project filters out the new Bitdefender VHDs, filters disallowed characters in local account names, improves Microsoft Dev Drive detection, improves the pre-formatting partition cleanup code, improves error reporting on ISO extraction issues, improves detection of drives with long hardware IDs (typically SSDs), improves conflicting process reporting, improves support for Nutanix and umbrelOS ISOs, fixes a TOCTOU vulnerability in Fido script execution (CVE-2026-2398), fixes replacement vulnerabilities for diskcopy.dll and oscdimg.exe, fixes FFU image creation being erroneously invocated when trying to save an ISO image, fixes saving of ISO images to paths that contain spaces, and updates UEFI:NTFS and UEFI DBXs to latest.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.13 [BUGFIX RELEASE]
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.13, the project fixes UEFI:NTFS not selecting the proper driver for ARM/ARM64, and updates embedded GRUB to v2.14.

chunks.title: Rufus 4.14
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the pbatard/rufus release v4.14, the project adds Windows User Experience improvements: a "Quality of Life" option to disable Teams, Outlook, Copilot and other Microsoft forced nuisances, a Silent installation option that automatically and without prompt installs Windows on the first detected disk on the target platform, an option to copy SkuSiPolicy.p7b to the ESP on installation, and tooltips for all the dialog options; adds limited support for El-Torito UEFI image extraction (mostly for Dell BIOS update ISOs), improves error report when the user tries to use an image that resides on the target drive, improves the UEFI:NTFS partition label to make the install media more explicit during Windows Setup disk partitioning, improves support for Bazzite and other Fedora derivatives that don't follow EFI conventions, improves reporting of GRUB and Isolinux MBRs, improves detection and exclusion of the new Bitdefender hidden VHDs, fixes potential errors during creation of Windows To Go media due to the use of new versions of bcdboot, and fixes errors with local accounts that start or end with whitespaces.

questions.query_text: In the pbatard/rufus releases, which release adds a new selection dialog for Windows 11 setup customization that includes bypassing the mandatory Microsoft account requirement for Windows 11 22H2?

questions.query_text: Across the pbatard/rufus releases, how does the Windows 11 in-place upgrade bypass in v4.6 differ from the Windows 11 setup customization dialog introduced in v3.19?

options.text: v4.6 adds a setup.exe wrapper to bypass Windows 11 24H2 in-place upgrade restrictions, while v3.19 adds a dialog that includes bypassing the Microsoft account requirement for Windows 11 22H2.

Both releases add the same setup.exe wrapper for in-place upgrades.
v4.6 adds a dialog for Microsoft account bypass, while v3.19 adds a setup.exe wrapper.

questions.expected_answer: v4.6 adds a setup.exe wrapper to bypass Windows 11 24H2 in-place upgrade restrictions, while v3.19 adds a dialog that includes bypassing the Microsoft account requirement for Windows 11 22H2.
