In the radareorg/radare2 release 6.0.6, the project replaces the old RStr.pad() with pad2, uses code/call/data refs to find shortest flow path, improves support for anal.timeout, handles more arm64 jump tables, exposes ptrsize on more arm LOADS, handles more cjmp instructions for loongson, falls back to recursive esil for too sparse functions, properly exposes ADD imm on arm64, fills op.val on arm64 CMP instructions, fixes p8fm mask size mismatch for instructions longer than 8 bytes, adds comprehensive ROP gadget tests for ARM32/ARM64/x86-64, fixes duplicate xrefs in axff output, uses 8MB stack for RThreads, exposes LOAD size for arm64 LDR ops, implements simple arena memory allocator, fixes wasm opsize read issue, assembles msub, str and stur ARM64 instructions, supports encoding ex9.it, ifret and ifcall nds32 instructions, adds register alias names for nds32, throws more ESIL and pseudo for nds32 instructions, adds support for v1/v2/v3 sBPF bytecode standards, describes all instructions for COSMAC architecture, supports assembling notrack r{jmp|call} prefix for x86-64, implements x86 assembler for pushfq/popfq and fixes cwde, fixes registers name for NDS32, imports hppa pseudo parser, adds HPPA disassembler database with instruction descriptions, adds instructionset documentation for nds32, imports nds32 pseudo parser, fixes ARM64 variable substitution in address calculation instructions, fixes compound assignments for ARM64 pseudo, supports asm.pseudo for x86 BMI1 instructions, assembles BMI1 instructions for x86-64, fixes pseudocode for arm64 movk instruction, adds more arm32 instruction descriptions, assembles movsz and movzx for x86-64, and adds support for ghost nops for x86-{32,64}.
In the radareorg/radare2 release 6.0.7 codenamed "sixseven", the project fixes parsing of r2 -H$(VARNAME) without a space in the shell.

In the radareorg/radare2 release 6.0.8 codenamed CleanWheat, the project migrates r_vector to RVec in core, anal, io, and other components, unifies redundant state vars in type propagation, uses Action Pack fixes routes with :: in the path and maintains Rack 2 parameter parsing. Railties fixes incorrect database.yml with skip_solid and sets Regexp.timeout to 1s by default.

In the rails/rails release 7.1.5, Active Model fixes a regression in alias_attribute to work with user-defined methods. Active Record fixes marshalling of unsaved associated records, an issue with left_outer_joins with multiple associations, ensures ActiveRecord::Encryption.config is always ready, and adds TimeZoneConverter#== method.

In the rails/rails release 7.2.2, Active Support includes options when instrumenting cache delete operations and prints test names for parallel tests. Active Model fixes alias_attribute regression. Active Record addresses query_cache: false support, sets .attributes_for_inspect to :all by default, makes PG::UnableToSend retryable, fixes marshalling of unsaved records, incorrect SQL with empty hash insert, polymorphic join table saving, association scopes on polymorphic has_many through, dependent: :destroy for bi-directional has one through, lazily pinned connection pools, Base.with with more than two sub queries, pinned connections with non-joinable connections, Float distinction in PostgreSQL, left_outer_joins with multiple associations, and ensures ActiveRecord::Encryption.config is always ready.

In the rails/rails release 8.0.0, Active Support removes deprecated support for passing array of strings to Deprecation#warn, setting attr_internal_naming_format with @ prefix, and ProxyObject. Action Pack fixes routes with :: and maintains Rack 2 parsing. Railties fixes database.yml with skip_solid and sets Regexp.timeout.

prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent react/create-react-app release stream from v2.0.4 through v5.0.1, covering major features like TypeScript support, Hooks, Fast Refresh, and webpack 5, along with numerous maintenance releases.

chunks.title: v2.0.4
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.0.4, the project fixes code minifying, fixes GENERATE_SOURCEMAP for CSS sourcemaps, disables Symbol typeof transform, caches Yarn resolution for faster installs, adds a version check for --use-pnp, adds .mjs support back to webpack, and includes various documentation updates.

chunks.title: v2.0.5
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.0.5, the project fixes click-to-open on Windows, fixes file size report after build, fixes CI for non-semver Yarn versions, fixes TypeError when registering service workers without config, uses correct dependency for babel-plugin-dynamic-import-node, adds environment variable to optionally disable inlining of chunks, updates eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v2.1.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.0, the project adds support for TypeScript, including TypeScript app creation via --typescript flag and TypeScript support using Babel 7, along with various TypeScript-related bug fixes and enhancements.

chunks.title: v2.1.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.1, the project adds support for decorators in TypeScript files, fixes a 'Duplicate string index signature' in ProcessEnv, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v2.1.2
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.2, the project adds allowESModules option to babel-preset-react-app, disables copy to clipboard in create-react-app --info, updates envinfo, fixes TypeScript decorator support, fixes named-asset-import plugin, avoids polyfilling fetch for Node, bumps postcss-preset-env, fixes tsconfig.json lib suggested value, adds support for setupTests.ts, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v2.1.3
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.3, the project updates webpack-dev-server to fix a vulnerability, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v2.1.4
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.4, the project reduces TypeScript rebuild times, adds Jest typeahead support, adds Sass source maps for dev, allows react-scripts test --no-watch, enables eval-source-map for Firefox, and includes various bug fixes and documentation updates.

chunks.title: v2.1.5
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.5, the project reverts the TypeScript speed improvements to fix a dependency issue in react-dev-utils.

chunks.title: v2.1.6
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.6, the project reintroduces reduced TypeScript rebuild times, reverts CSS sourcemaps in development, reverts eval-source-map, adds forward ref to React SVG Component, uses contenthash for better long-term caching, and includes various bug fixes and documentation updates.

chunks.title: v2.1.7
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.7, the project temporarily reverts the TypeScript speed improvements to fix a dependency issue in react-dev-utils.

chunks.title: v2.1.8
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v2.1.8, the project reapplies the TypeScript speed improvements in a new major version of react-dev-utils.

chunks.title: v3.0.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.0.0, the project introduces support for Hooks, Jest 24, TypeScript linting, browserslist support in @babel/preset-env, absolute imports using jsconfig.json/tsconfig.json, PostCSS Normalize, and includes breaking changes such as new ESLint rules for Hooks, TypeScript linting, removal of --no-watch flag, and new asset-manifest.json structure.

chunks.title: v3.0.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.0.1, the project adjusts ESLint rules for TypeScript, unpins babel-jest, changes CSS module classname hash to use relative paths, adds configuration for PnP/TypeScript, generates SVG component name in Jest fileTransform, removes body padding reset from templates, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v3.1.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.1.0, the project adds ESLint 6 support, experimental ESLint config customization, more Jest config options, option to configure or disable image inlining, handles browser arguments, fixes HMR in Firefox with proxy, resolves relative paths for preprocessor styles, and includes various bug fixes and enhancements.

chunks.title: v3.1.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.1.1, the project fixes ESLint 6 support, stops blocking static files in robots.txt, ignores jsx-a11y/aria-role for React components, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v3.1.2
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.1.2, the project changes runtime chunk name separator from tilde to dash, explicitly checks EXTEND_ESLINT, fixes build, adds new logo, makes minor performance improvements, disables babel-loader's cacheCompression, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v3.2.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.2.0, the project adds support for production profiling with React Developer Tools, adds TSC_COMPILE_ON_ERROR env var to ignore TypeScript type errors, fixes linting error with rest props, guards polyfills against undefined window, supports setting baseUrl to root directory, only loads eslint config when EXTEND_ESLINT is specified, sets output.globalObject to 'this', adds entrypoints key to asset manifest, enables .eslintignore again, stops hiding column number of ESLint errors, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v3.3.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.3.0, the project introduces custom templates, support for optional chaining and nullish coalescing operators, numeric separators, removes no-unexpected-multiline rule, and deprecates --typescript flag in favor of --template typescript.

chunks.title: v3.3.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.3.1, the project adds Disallow to robots.txt, fixes sass importLoaders, adds titleProp to SVGR ReactComponent type definition, proactively appends to .gitignore during generation, fixes CSS font-face minification, syncs babel config dependencies, adds slashes to WebSocket protocol URL, uses wss when https is used, adds helpful message to error overlay footer, removes React.FC from TypeScript template, adds template support for any package.json keys, supports shorthand scoped templates, adds current version and bin location to --info output, replaces favicon in templates, removes error for @typescript-eslint/no-namespace, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v3.4.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.4.0, the project downgrades style-loader to fix CSS modules hot reload, downgrades chalk for IE 11 support, fixes unchecked access to deploy script, handles service worker error in Firefox, fixes robots.txt for TypeScript template, does not redirect served path if request may proxy, allows PUBLIC_URL in development mode, enables custom sockjs pathname for hot reloading, changes arrow functions to function declarations in TypeScript template, adds option to provide custom SSL certificates during development, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v3.4.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.4.1, the project uses native ESLint behaviour when extending, closes webpack dev server on end stdin, fixes optional chaining and nullish coalescing support, widens eslint-config-react-app peer dependency versions, adds React.StrictMode to default templates, allows specification of package.main in template.json, updates to Babel 7.9, and bumps dependencies.

chunks.title: v3.4.2
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.4.2, the project bumps webpack-dev-server to a version without npm audit vulnerability.

chunks.title: v3.4.3
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.4.3, the project bumps terser-webpack-plugin to a version without npm audit vulnerability.

chunks.title: v3.4.4
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v3.4.4, the project bumps resolve-url-loader to a version without npm audit vulnerability.

chunks.title: v4.0.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v4.0.0, the project introduces Fast Refresh, React 17 support, new JSX transform, TypeScript 4 support, ESLint 7, new Jest and React Testing Library rules, Jest 26, PWA/workbox improvements including switch to Workbox InjectManifest plugin and separate template, Web Vitals support, AVIF image support, and includes breaking changes such as ESLint 7 upgrade, Jest 26 with resetMocks true by default, service worker changes, removal of deprecated typescript flag and NODE_PATH support, fix dotenv file loading order, and dropped Node 8 support.

chunks.title: v4.0.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v4.0.1, the project fixes noFallthroughCasesInSwitch/jsx object is not extensible, fixes react-jsx error, fixes React is not defined compilation error after ejected, fixes slow recompile time, fixes page not refreshing when FAST_REFRESH=false, increases Workbox's maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v4.0.2
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v4.0.2, the project adds support for new BUILD_PATH advanced configuration variable, adds opt-out for eslint-webpack-plugin, adds missing peer dependency react and updates react-refresh-webpack-plugin, adds TypeScript 4.x as peerDependency to react-scripts, moves ESLint cache file into node_modules, improves vendor chunk names in development, and includes documentation updates.

chunks.title: v4.0.3
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v4.0.3, the project upgrades eslint-webpack-plugin to fix opt-out flag, updates immer to address vulnerability, and updates test case.

chunks.title: v5.0.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the react/create-react-app release v5.0.0, the project upgrades to webpack 5, Jest 27, ESLint 8, PostCSS 8, improves Fast Refresh, adds support for Tailwind, improves package manager detection, unpins all dependencies, drops support for Node 10 and 12, deprecates root level template.json keys, disables overlay for warnings, fixes ICSS syntax in stylesheets, adds source-map-loader, removes ESLint verification when opting-out, and includes various other enhancements.

chunks.title: v5.0.1

prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent redis/redis release stream across multiple major and minor versions, including security patches, new features like atomic slot migration and hybrid search, and performance improvements.

chunks.memory_unit_text: In the redis/redis release 8.0.4, the project addresses several security vulnerabilities including CVE-2025-49844, CVE-2025-46817, CVE-2025-46818, and CVE-2025-46819 related to Lua scripts. It introduces a new EPSILON argument for the VSIM command to specify maximum distance. Bug fixes include potential use-after-free after pubsub and Lua defrag, potential crash on Lua script defrag, HINCRBYFLOAT removing field expiration on replica, preventing CLIENT UNBLOCK from unblocking CLIENT PAUSE, endless client blocking for blocking commands, vector sets RDB format incompatibility with big endian machines, EVAL crash when error table is empty, and graceful handling of short read errors for hashes with TTL during full sync.

In the redis/redis release 8.2.2, the project addresses the same Lua-related security vulnerabilities as 8.0.4. It adds the EPSILON argument to VSIM and introduces Intel optimizations for SVS-VAMANA via a build flag. Bug fixes include potential crash on Lua script defrag, potential crash on streams and HFE defrag, potential use-after-free after pubsub and Lua defrag, MEMORY USAGE reporting fix, limiting ENTRIESREAD value in XGROUP CREATE/SETID, JSON.DEL not deleting all matching members, TDIGEST.CREATE crash on huge initialization values, potential shard restart while reindexing vectors on RDB loading, potential crash with small CONSTRUCTION_WINDOW_SIZE on SVS-VAMANA, potential crash due to file descriptor leak, potential crash when using ACL rules, incorrect vector index memory value in INFO SEARCH, and more accurate execution duration measurements in FT.PROFILE. Performance improvements include better RESP3 serialization, and new SVS-VAMANA metrics are added to INFO SEARCH.
In the redis/redis release 6.2.21, the update urgency is HIGH due to a critical bug that may affect a subset of users. The release fixes a potential crash on HyperLogLog with 2GB+ entries.
In the redis/redis release 7.2.12, the update urgency is HIGH due to a critical bug that may affect a subset of users. The release fixes a potential crash on HyperLogLog with 2GB+ entries.
In the redis/redis release 7.4.7, the update urgency is HIGH due to a critical bug that may affect a subset of users. The release fixes a potential crash on HyperLogLog with 2GB+ entries.

In the redis/redis release 8.0.5, the update urgency is HIGH due to critical bugs that may affect a subset of users. Bug fixes include a potential crash in HGETEX when FIELDS is used and numfields is missing, potential crash on HyperLogLog with 2GB+ entries, division by zero in Cuckoo filter insertion, counter overflow in Cuckoo filter, arbitrary memory read/write with invalid Bloom filter, out-of-bounds access with empty chain in Bloom filter, restore invalid Bloom filter (thanks to AWS security), and out-of-bounds access in Top-k.

In the redis/redis release 8.2.3, the update urgency is SECURITY due to a security fix for CVE-2025-62507, a potential stack overflow and RCE in XACKDEL. Bug fixes include potential crash in HGETEX when FIELDS is used and numfields is missing, potential crash on HyperLogLog with 2GB+ entries, division by zero in Cuckoo filter insertion, counter overflow in Cuckoo filter, arbitrary memory read/write with invalid Bloom filter, out-of-bounds access with empty chain in Bloom filter, restore invalid Bloom filter (thanks to AWS security), and out-of-bounds access in Top-k.

chunks.title: 8.4-RC1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the redis/redis release 8.4-RC1, this is the first Release Candidate of Redis 8.4. New features compared to 8.2.3 include CLUSTER MIGRATION for atomic slot migration, DELEX and DIGEST commands with SET extensions for atomic compare-and-set and compare-and-delete, MSETEX for setting multiple keys with expiration, XREADGROUP CLAIM min-idle-time to consume idle pending and incoming entries, auto-repair options for broken AOF tail on startup, support for decoding JSON empty array as a Lua array, HELP and COMMAND DOCS support for time series and probabilistic commands, FT.HYBRID for hybrid queries with RRF and LINEAR combination, support for index updates during atomic slot migrations, and multiple I/O threads for RQE cluster manager. Bug fixes include potential infinite loop on corrupted stream, shutdown blocked client not properly reset, heap-buffer-overflow in CLUSTER FORGET, potential crash in lookupKey when executing_client is NULL, and potential crash on TS.RANGE with ALIGN +, AGGREGATION twa and EMPTY. Performance improvements include lookahead prefetching, optimized BITCOUNT with AVX2/AVX512 and Arm Neon SIMD, optimized HyperLogLog with branchless comparisons and Arm Neon SIMD, optimized Vector set VADD and VSIM with AVX2/AVX512 dot product, and JSON memory footprint improvements. New configuration parameters include aof-load-corrupt-tail-max-size, decode_array_with_array_mt, lookahead, search-default-scorer, search-on-oom, and search-io-threads.

In the redis/redis release 8.4.0, this is the General Availability release of Redis 8.4. Major changes compared to 8.2 include DIGEST, DELEX, and SET extensions for atomic compare-and-set and compare-and-delete, MSETEX for atomically setting multiple string keys with expiration, XREADGROUP with new CLAIM option, CLUSTER MIGRATION for atomic slot migration, CLUSTER SLOT-STATS for per-slot usage metrics, FT.HYBRID for hybrid search and fused scoring, I/O threading for search and query commands, substantial throughput increase (e.g., >30% for caching use cases), and JSON memory reduction for homogenous arrays (up to 92%). Bug fixes compared to 8.4-RC1 include XREADGROUP CLAIM returning strings instead of integers, adding variable key-spec flags to SET IF* and DELEX, potential memory leak, macOS build failures, JSON.NUMINCRBY wrong result on integer array with non-integer increment, and thread safety issue related to ASM and shared strings. Performance improvements include optimizing XREADGROUP. Known bugs and limitations include partial or duplicate results during atomic slot migration for certain commands, missing FT.HYBRID option in FT.PROFILE/FT.EXPLAIN/FT.EXPLACINCLI, missing metrics from FT.HYBRID, unsupported options in FT.HYBRID, and unsupported post-filtering.

chunks.title: 8.6-RC1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the redis/redis release 8.6-RC1, this is the first Release Candidate of Redis 8.6. New features compared to 8.4.0 include XADD idempotency with IDMPAUTO and IDMP arguments, new eviction policies volatile-lrm and allkeys-lrm, hot keys detection and reporting with the HOTKEYS command, TLS certificate-based automatic client authentication, and time series support for NaN values with new aggregators COUNTNAN and COUNTALL. Security and privacy fixes include hiding Personally Identifiable Information from ACL log, ACL key-pattern bypass in MSETEX, hiding PII from server log, and out-of-bounds read when loading an invalid RDB file. Bug fixes include ACL AOF loading failure, atomic slot migration wrong adjacent slot range behavior, support delay trimming slots, XTRIM/XADD with approx mode not deleting entries, incorrect behavior with XDELEX...ACKED after XGROUP DESTROY, SCAN filter order restoration, rare server hang at shutdown, panic when cluster node is uninitialized, FLUSHALL ASYNC blocking main thread, race condition in broadcast configuration, fixed argument position handling, atomic slot migration support for modules, MEMORY USAGE fix, adding escapes to already-escaped characters, and JSON.CLEAR not erroring on multiple paths. Performance improvements include reply copy-avoidance, unifying hash field name and value, unifying sorted set score and value, optimizing listpack iterator, optimizing set commands with expiration, optimizing prefetching, optimizing ZRANK, utilizing hardware clock on ARM, and disabling RDB compression during diskless replication. New Modules API functions are introduced for key metadata management. Configuration parameters include cluster-slot-stats-enabled and key-memory-histograms.

In the redis/redis release 8.2.4, the update urgency is SECURITY. Security fixes include hiding Personally Identifiable Information from server log. prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent rust-lang/rust release stream from version 1.75.0 through 1.96.0, including minor and patch releases. It captures language stabilizations, compiler improvements, library additions, and platform support changes across the evolution of the Rust compiler and standard library.

chunks.title: Rust 1.75.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.75.0, the project stabilizes async fn and return-position impl Trait in traits, allows function pointer signatures containing &mut T in const contexts, and matches usize/isize exhaustively with half-open ranges. The compiler reworks negative coherence, bumps COINDUCTIVE_OVERLAP_IN_COHERENCE to deny, and adds several tier 3 targets. Libraries override Waker::clone_from, implement BufRead for VecDeque<u8>, and support sub-millisecond sleep on Windows. Stabilized APIs include Atomic*::from_ptr, FileTimes, and IpAddr::to_canonical.

chunks.title: Rust 1.76.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.76.0, the language documents Rust ABI compatibility between various types and guarantees that char and u32 are ABI-compatible. The compiler adds a lint for pinned #[must_use] pointers, fixes soundness issues with packed structs, and adds tier 3 targets including aarch64-apple-watchos. Libraries add a column number to dbg!(), export std::hash::{DefaultHasher, RandomState}, and allow File::create to work on hidden files on Windows. Stabilized APIs include Arc::unwrap_or_clone, Result::inspect, and ptr::addr_eq.

chunks.title: Rust 1.77.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.77.0, the language stabilizes C-string literals and THIR unsafeck, adds a static_mut_refs lint, and supports async recursive calls with indirection. The compiler makes i128 and u128 16-byte aligned on x86, merges unused_tuple_struct_fields into dead_code, and promotes riscv32 targets to tier 2. Libraries implement From<&[T; N]> for Cow<[T]>. Stabilized APIs include array::each_ref, core::net, and mem::offset_of!.

chunks.title: Rust 1.77.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.77.1, the project reverts stripping debuginfo by default for Windows, fixing a regression introduced in 1.77.0. An internal fix addresses heading anchor rendering in doc pages.

chunks.title: Rust 1.77.2
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.77.2, the project addresses CVE-2024-24576 by fixing escaping of Windows batch file arguments in std::process::Command.

chunks.title: Rust 1.78.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.78.0, the language stabilizes #[diagnostic] namespace and #[diagnostic::on_unimplemented], makes matching on NaN a hard error, and allows upcasting from dyn Trait to dyn Trait + Auto. The compiler makes INVALID_DOC_ATTRIBUTES deny by default, requires Windows 10 for tier 1 Windows targets, and adds wasm32-wasip1 tier 2 target. Libraries bump Unicode to version 15.1.0. Stabilized APIs include impl Task for &Task and impl FromIterator for (impl Default + Extend, impl Default + Extend).

chunks.title: Rust 1.79.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.79.0, the language stabilizes inline const {} expressions, associated type bounds (RFC 2289), and importing main from other modules. The compiler stabilizes -Crelro-level and --check-cfg, and promotes several Windows targets to tier 2. Libraries implement FromIterator for tuples and enable frame pointers for the standard library. Stabilized APIs include {integer}::unchecked_add and {integer}::unchecked_mul.

chunks.title: Rust 1.80.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.80.0, the language stabilizes exclusive_range_pattern, supports C23's variadics without a named parameter, and guarantees layout and ABI of Result in some scenarios. The compiler adds a lint against never type fallback affecting unsafe code and adds x86_64-unknown-linux-none as a tier 3 target. Libraries add size_of and align_of to the prelude and raise DEFAULT_MIN_STACK_SIZE to at least 64KiB. Stabilized APIs include impl Default for Rc<CStr> and impl IntoIterator for Box<[T]>.

chunks.title: Rust 1.80.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.80.1, the project fixes a miscompilation in the jump threading MIR optimization when comparing floats and reverts changes to the dead_code lint from 1.80.0.

chunks.title: Rust 1.81.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.81.0, the language stabilizes #[expect] for lints (RFC 2383), aborts on uncaught panics in extern "C" functions, and denies keyword lifetimes pre-expansion. The compiler makes casts of pointers to trait objects stricter and adds tier 3 Xtensa targets. Libraries replace sort implementations with stable driftsort and unstable ipnsort for significant performance improvements. Stabilized APIs include core::error::Error and impl Default for Rc<str>.

chunks.title: Rust 1.82.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.82.0, the language stabilizes &raw const and &raw mut operators (RFC 2582), unsafe extern blocks (RFC 3484), and floating-point arithmetic in const fn. The compiler promotes aarch64-apple-darwin to Tier 1 and wasm32-wasip2 to Tier 2. Libraries generalize {Rc,Arc}::make_mut() to Path, OsStr, and CStr. Stabilized APIs include std::thread::Builder::spawn_unchecked and [T]::is_sorted.

chunks.title: Rust 1.83.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.83.0, the language stabilizes &mut, *mut, &Cell, and *const Cell in const, implements raw lifetimes and labels ('r#ident), and stabilizes expr_2021 macro fragment specifier. The compiler deprecates unsound -Csoft-float flag and adds many new tier 3 targets. Libraries bump Unicode to version 16.0.0. Stabilized APIs include BufRead::skip_until and ControlFlow::break_value.

chunks.title: Rust 1.84.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.84.0, the language uses the next-generation trait solver in coherence, stabilizes s390x and Arm64EC inline assembly, and executes drop glue when unwinding in an extern "C" function. The compiler adds --print host-tuple flag and stabilizes WebAssembly multivalue, reference-types, and tail-call target features. Libraries implement From<&mut {slice}> for Box/Rc/Arc<{slice}> and make std::os::darwin public. Stabilized APIs include Ipv6Addr::is_unique_local and <int>::isqrt.

chunks.title: Rust 1.84.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.84.1, the project fixes an ICE in duplicate-crate diagnostics, errors for overlapping impls in incremental rebuilds, slow compilation related to the next-generation trait solver, and debuginfo when LLVM's location discriminator value limit is exceeded. It also includes fixes for building Rust from source.

chunks.title: Rust 1.85.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.85.0, the 2024 Edition is now stable. The language stabilizes async closures and #[diagnostic::do_not_recommend], and adds an unpredictable_function_pointer_comparisons lint. The compiler removes the unstable -Zpolymorphize flag. Libraries make panics in the standard library have a leading library/ in their path. Stabilized APIs include BuildHasherDefault::new and ptr::fn_addr_eq.

chunks.title: Rust 1.85.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.85.1, the project fixes the doctest-merging feature of the 2024 Edition, relaxes some target_feature checks when generating docs, fixes errors in std::fs::rename on Windows 10 version 1607, downgrades bootstrap cc to fix custom targets, and skips submodule updates when building Rust from a source tarball.

chunks.title: Rust 1.86.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.86.0, the language stabilizes upcasting trait objects to supertraits, allows safe functions to be marked with #[target_feature], and adds a double_negations lint. The compiler changes -O to mean -C opt-level=3 and debug-asserts that raw pointers are non-null on access. Libraries change FromBytesWithNulError from an opaque struct to an enum. Stabilized APIs include {float}::next_down and {float}::next_up.

chunks.title: Rust 1.87.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.87.0, the language stabilizes asm_goto feature and precise_capturing_in_traits allowing use<...> bounds on return position impl Trait in traits. The compiler makes SSE2 required for i686 targets. Libraries stabilize the anonymous pipe API and add support for unbounded left/right shift operations. Stabilized APIs include Vec::extract_if and io::pipe.

chunks.title: Rust 1.88.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.88.0, the language stabilizes let_chains in the 2024 edition, naked_functions, and cfg_boolean_literals. It fully de-stabilizes the #[bench] attribute and adds a dangerous_implicit_autorefs lint. The compiler stabilizes -Cdwarf-version. Libraries guarantee that {float}::NAN is a quiet NaN. Stabilized APIs include Cell::update and HashMap::extract_if.

chunks.title: Rust 1.89.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.89.0, the language stabilizes explicitly inferred const arguments (generic_arg_infer), avx512 target features, and repr128. It adds a mismatched_lifetime_syntaxes lint and makes dangerous_implicit_autorefs deny-by-default. The compiler defaults to non-leaf frame pointers on aarch64-linux. Libraries allow storing format_args!() in a variable. Stabilized APIs include NonZero<char> and File::lock.

chunks.title: Rust 1.90.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.90.0, the language splits up the unknown_or_malformed_diagnostic_attributes lint into four finer-grained lints and allows volatile access to non-Rust memory. The compiler uses lld by default on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. Libraries stabilize u*::{checked,overflowing,saturating,wrapping}_sub_signed. Stabilized APIs include u{n}::checked_sub_signed and impl PartialEq<&CStr> for CStr.

chunks.title: Rust 1.91.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.91.0, the language stabilizes declaration of C-style variadic functions for sysv64, win64, efiapi, and aapcs ABIs, and adds a dangling_pointers_from_locals lint. The compiler doesn't warn on never-to-any as casts as unreachable. Libraries print thread ID in panic message. Stabilized APIs include Path::file_prefix and AtomicPtr::fetch_ptr_add.

chunks.title: Rust 1.91.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.91.1, the project enables file locking support in illumos and fixes the wasm_import_module attribute cross-crate to resolve linker errors on WASM targets.

chunks.title: Rust 1.92.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.92.0, the language documents MaybeUninit representation and validity, allows &raw [mut | const] for union field in safe code, and makes never type lints deny-by-default. The compiler removes current code for embedding command-line args in PDB. Libraries specialize Iterator::eq{_by} for TrustedLen iterators. Stabilized APIs include NonZero<u{N}>::div_ceil and Box::new_zeroed.

chunks.title: Rust 1.93.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.93.0, the language stabilizes several s390x vector-related target features and asm_cfg, and adds a function_casts_as_integer lint. The compiler stabilizes -Cjump-tables=bool. Libraries stop internally using specialization on the Copy trait. Stabilized APIs include <[MaybeUninit<T>]>::assume_init_drop and String::into_raw_parts.

chunks.title: Rust 1.93.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.93.1, the project fixes an ICE that affected rustfmt by not trying to recover keyword as non-keyword identifier, fixes a clippy false-positive, and reverts a wasm-related CI update to fix file descriptor leaks on wasm32-wasip2.

chunks.title: Rust 1.94.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.94.0, the language stabilizes additional 29 RISC-V target features and updates to Unicode 17. Libraries relax T: Ord bound for some BinaryHeap<T> methods. Stabilized APIs include <[T]>::array_windows and LazyCell::get.

chunks.title: Rust 1.94.1
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.94.1, the project fixes std::thread::spawn on wasm32-wasip1-threads, removes new unstable methods from std::os::windows::fs::OpenOptionsExt, fixes a clippy ICE, and updates tar to resolve CVEs.

chunks.title: Rust 1.95.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.95.0, the language stabilizes if let guards on match arms and inline assembly for PowerPC and PowerPC64. The compiler stabilizes --remap-path-scope. Libraries speed up str::contains on aarch64 targets with neon. Stabilized APIs include MaybeUninit<[T; N]>: From<[MaybeUninit<T>; N]>.

chunks.title: Rust 1.96.0
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rust-lang/rust release 1.96.0, the language allows passing expr metavariable to cfg and supports s390x vector registers in inline assembly. The compiler enables link relaxation for LoongArch Linux targets. Libraries support iterating over ranges of NonZero integers. Stabilized APIs include assert_matches! and core::range::RangeToInclusive.

prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent rustdesk/rustdesk release stream from 1.1.8 through 1.4.6, including major feature additions like Flutter rewrite, Wayland support, web client, and cross-platform improvements.

chunks.memory_unit_text: In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.1.8, the project adds an iOS client, touch screen mode for mobile clients, support for 32-bit Windows (>=Win7), and enables dxgi with fallback to gdi. It also fixes compatibility issues, mouse/keyboard behaviors, clipboard sync on Linux, and upgrades tokio to v1 and vpx to 1.10. Additionally, it experiments with Wayland support (temporarily given up), provides a Windows setup exe with an option to run without installation, and adds small features like preset RDP username/password and prohibiting remote modification of local configuration.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.1.9, the project introduces a web client (Beta, for Chrome), Mac background service (privileged to work on login screen), Sock5 support, control of Android devices (with known capture issues on some devices), international keyboard support (Beta), enhanced security, LAN discovery (Beta), an Address Book (Beta), a better session list page, and various bug fixes.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.0, the project is rewritten with Flutter and adds IPv6 support (beta), strengthened password, quick support feature, hardware codecs H264/H265 (beta), AV1 codec, international keyboard (map mode and translate mode), Wayland support (beta, with known issues), privacy mode (beta, Windows only), headless Linux support, virtual display (Windows), resolution adjustment, dark theme, and many other improvements.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.1, the project fixes several issues including email login verification bugs on mobile, privacy broker zombie process, and various UI and chat notification refactors on mobile and desktop. It also improves the remote menubar, adjusts tab theme, and refactors the ID input box on mobile.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.2, the project adds a separate window mode (tab window by default), fixes and improves responsiveness issues introduced in 1.2.0, adds device list batch handling, adds a command to assign user and strategy for RustDesk Server Pro, optimizes the address book with syncing password, alias name, device name, tag color, and improved error/update status handling, fixes Windows file copy/paste, fixes a 'waiting for image...' bug, improves touchpad support, and includes other bug fixes.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.3, the project improves Wayland support (cursor, clipboard, multi-monitors, but highly depends on Xwayland, works well on GNOME, bad compatibility on KDE), adds a group tab, adds software update check based on GitHub latest tag, includes some fixes for Kaspersky compliance, and includes many other fixes since 1.2.2. Work continues on dual-monitors-dual-windows and new hardware codecs for 1.2.4.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.3-1, the project fixes a RustDesk certificate vulnerability reported by incibe-es, impacting x86-64 Windows version only. The release updates the x86-64 Windows executable and provides instructions to fix the vulnerability by uninstalling, upgrading, or manually removing the test certificate. It also provides an alternative way to install virtual display.
In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.3-2, the project only fixes a bug introduced in 1.2.3-1 related to wrong certificate stores in certmgr.msc.
In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.4, the project provides a pre-release for testing, with no detailed changelog provided in the release notes.
In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.5, the project provides a pre-release for testing, with no detailed changelog provided in the release notes.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.6, the project adds removal of desktop wallpaper on Windows and Linux, dual screen dual windows support, writing log on Android to external storage for audit, auto reconnect improvement, autocomplete in ID input box, AV1 record (with a slight backward compatibility break), single peer per row/list view, and many fixes including Wayland fixes, and other bug fixes.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.2.7, the project adds shared image of clipboard, Sciter version of Linux x64 deb and flatpak, loading window for portable Windows, more options for custom client, Android actions to menu, Telegram 2FA and notification, set clipboard text of controlled Android, macOS hardware codecs, and view mode/resolution change/virtual display/proxy etc to mobile. It also removes confusing 'Connection not allowed' popup and includes other changes and fixes.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.0, the project adds multi clipboard formats (html/rtf), send clipboard keystroke, active tab border, MSI options for desktop and start menu shortcuts, add client to address book/tag via command line, universal apk, unlock with pin, 'Trust this device' option for 2FA, and rename file and folder in file transfer window. It also changes window position keeping after new connection, vcpkg ffmpeg, removes autostart entry of '--tray' on Linux, uses JNI MediaCodec-backed hardware codecs on Android, removes virtual displays on disconnection, and fixes reversed left/right wheel, huge memory usage, and other issues.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.1, the project adds four new advanced options: one-way-clipboard-redirection/one-way-file-transfer, sync-init-clipboard, and allow-logon-screen-password. It optimizes desktop file manager UI and status list, makes UI responsive, changes libappindicator to libayatana-appindicator, disables clipboard init sync, and fixes a new cm tab not replacing old persisted tab issue introduced in 1.2.7, among other fixes.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.2, the project adds a Web client v2 Preview, auto record outgoing sessions, and map mode from mobile physical keyboard to desktop. It changes the need to input password again if opening file transfer from remote window, and fixes issues including 'Check for software update on startup' not working, shared address book swap on iOS, no history/favorites, Windows restore/maximize, missing bc dependency, copy and paste limited in 1.3.1, file transfer not working on controlled side in Flatpak, Windows multi-window move between monitors, and Wayland capslock.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.3, the project adds rotate ID3D11Texture2D, ensure cursor visible when software keyboard pops out, mobile clipboard support, system sound of Mac arm, and 'Untagged' to filter address book peers without tags. It upgrades to Flutter 3.24 for better GPU compatibility, reverts Korean compose improvement, does not allow cursor out of canvas in mobile, removes y-pan limitation when soft keyboard appears, reverts default codec back to AV1, and fixes refresh button when random password disabled, save/restore window position, and other issues.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.4, the project adds mobile key help tool with more keys, changes 'Untagged' tag to use theme accent color, and Linux dynamic load libva for better compatibility. It fixes Windows 7 support (64-bit, service pack 1 required), Linuxmint window not displayed, keyboard input issues after pressing F4, cannot drag vertical slider in GUI, Android mouse mode swipe gesture, rounded corners opaque black after 1.3.3, and application crash on Mac when typing in ID/Relay server fields.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.5, the project provides urgent fixes for rustdesk 1.3.4 not showing GUI main window on openSUSE Leap 15.6 (only KDE tray icon and symbol) and unable to launch macOS client 1.3.3 or 1.3.4 due to missing referenced symbols in the objective-C dylib on OSX 12.7.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.6, the project improves macOS keyboard translate mode and fixes issues including bypass permission, pasted from clipboard toast notification on Android, multiple entries with poor internet connection, Windows host clipboard cleared when remote connection closed, SELinux, one hardware codec failure, double cursor on arm Mac introduced in 1.3.3, Linux mint freeze introduced in Flutter 3.24, pulse audio, mobile mouse mode right menu unexpected click, iOS no sound from remote Windows PC, and clipboard from browser to remote issues.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.7, the project adds new QoS, creates a separate executable for '--service' to avoid 'app not open any more' problem on Mac completely, and fixes Android update button cannot be clicked, image blur occurring at the moment of changing quality, and lock the zoom when controlling on Android device.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.8, the project adds cross platform file copy & paste (copy to macOS not ready yet), device group, allows dash in ID, changes right click behavior on controlled Android to long press, changes 'Group' tab to 'Accessible devices', and fixes Windows 10 and macOS window border, touch move for controlling Android from desktop and mobile, and freezes when clicking on ID line.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.3.9, the project adds remote printer (Windows to Windows only), view camera, copy file to macOS, support Citrix session, allow-https-21114 option, disables vram (D3D) decoder by default to avoid black screen on some desktops, changes MSI silent installation not to start client after installation, and fixes custom client wrong position of settings button, and one blank window case for multiple display switch.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.4.0, the project adds allow logon screen password on lock screen, take screenshot, hostname as ID for Pro, auto update on Windows and manual update on Windows and Mac, web socket support on all platforms, trackpad speed adjustment, removes system proxy dep of reqwest, capitalizes display name, only uses TCP in socks5 proxy, changes 'Exit' to 'Stop service' on tray, and fixes virtual F11 key to macOS, tray startup tried via sudo, http proxy with reqwest, hide cm, LAN discovery, RDP, mouse scroll and remote tabs, and 2FA login status.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.4.1, the project adds terminal, UDP and IPv6 punch, stylus, numeric one time password option, enable force-always-relay option in address books and accessible devices, forces secure TCP for login session, clears accessible devices tab when retrieving disabled, improves SAS, shortens retry time for some network errors, and fixes macOS resolution list for Retina, cannot input password if lock screen via RustDesk on macOS, key input lag on macOS, crash of 32 bit on Windows X64 for camera connection, len(uid) < 4 case, no icon for RustDesk AppImage, test nat type for outgoing-only client, untagged tag not working in secondary address books, bring back allow-https-21114, Linux nokhwa camera index, and Windows upload issues.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.4.2, the project adds show your cursor on controlled side in view mode, incremental file transfer support (both sides 1.4.2 required), sciter hide cm, show TCP/UDP/IPv6 in tooltip, clipboard files audit, advanced option main window always on top, disable-discovery-pane, address-book level password, tries UDP/TCP punch both at the same time, enhances .desktop file with new keywords, upgrades codecs, and fixes nokhwa win infinite loop, set allowMalformed to true when decode utf8, iOS file transfer home dir, Ubuntu activity name, audio delay on Linux, mouse event is in current window, scrambled image, and port forward invalid msg.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.4.3, the project adds virtual mouse on mobile, custom scale mode with inline controls and live apply, Wayland multi-monitor screen capture functionality, more assign from CLI and devices.py, address book API res/ab.py and audit API res/audits.py, IPv6 prefix-based rate limiting on login failures, centralizes debounce of save window pos and save window pos on close, moves touch mode option from peer to local, and fixes Arch/Wayland 100% CPU, low fps on macOS if running as service, window positioning on Windows when taskbar is on top or left, websocket reconnect, crash on Android armv7 (introduced in 1.4.1), uninstall idd, and portable program can't run from cmd on win7.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.4.4, the project adds better Wayland support for multi scaled monitors (Gnome and KDE), edge scrolling, ask for note at the end of connection, iOS allow transferred files to be managed by Files and iTunes, allow flipping sort order in mobile app's file transfer, file transfer auto start on reconnect, show proxy settings on iOS, load custom installed CA root on mobile, UI customization for Sciter version, insecure TLS option, macOS command line of update from dmg file, changes rustls-tls fall back to native-tls, changes http post in UI from Flutter to native rust, flatpak socket x11 for better compatibility, and fixes image paused for multiple incoming connections with multiple screens, camera capture large error log, macOS hwcodec check for both x64 and Arm64, scale custom on mobile, show alias instead of peerId in terminal tab label, reqwest proxy auth, macOS bigsur cvbuffer crash, keep chat window within screen bounds, and terminal clear command on some env.

In the rustdesk/rustdesk release 1.4.5, the project adds allow configuring remote control permissions for different users, relative mouse mode, terminal two-row floating keyboard buttons for common commands (mobile only), removes gzip encoding in Legacy AB pushes, shows login dialog when clicking note if not logged in, requires login for note, changes remote toolbar icon and show/hide, delegates win --server file reading to CM in file transfer, and fixes file transfer perm on access-mode, desktop wakelock issue with multiple tabs in same window, address book fetch failure, and other issues.

prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent ruvnet/RuView release stream, covering HOMECORE web UI iterations, streaming engine trust features, world model integration, and swarm control system additions.

chunks.title: v0.11.0 — HOMECORE in Docker + crate-level READMEs
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v0.11.0, the project publishes a polish and packaging update for the v0.10.0 HOMECORE work. The homecore-server binary is now included in the published Docker image alongside sensing-server and cog-ha-matter, with multi-arch support for amd64 and arm64. Comprehensive READMEs are added for every HOMECORE crate, each containing tagline, badges, feature lists, capability tables, comparisons to Home Assistant Python equivalents, performance notes, usage examples, and relation diagrams. All 2,263 workspace tests remain green.

chunks.title: Release v1397
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1397, an automated CI pipeline release adds a navigation router and three new pages to the HOMECORE web UI: States, Services, and Settings. The router maps navigation IDs to page custom elements, swapping the AppShell child on hc-navigate events. The States page shows an entity table with 5-second refresh, the Services page displays a domain-grouped service registry with an empty state, and the Settings page provides backend config readout and a bearer-token editor.

chunks.title: v0.12.0 — HOMECORE web UI is live + 9-phase verify Trust Kill Switch
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v0.12.0, the HOMECORE web UI becomes functional with new Dashboard, States, Services, and Settings pages, replacing the previous empty shell. The Dashboard fetches config and states, renders entity cards, and polls every 5 seconds. The Trust Kill Switch is expanded to a 9-phase verification covering v1, v2, and HOMECORE, including Rust workspace tests, PyO3 binding compilation, ADR-125 invariant checks, crate publishing, npm package, and multi-arch Docker manifest. Additional fixes address Pydantic secret leaks, numpy drift, and verification script bugs.

chunks.title: Release v1402
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1402, the homecore-server seeds 13 default services across 6 domains on boot, so the service registry is no longer empty on a vanilla start. Each handler echoes the call as a JSON acknowledgement. The seeded domains include homeassistant, light, switch, scene, automation, and homecore. The web UI Services page now shows these services under proper domain headings.

chunks.title: Release v1403
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1403, the homecore-server seeds 10 default entities on boot, mirroring the bash seed script, with a new --no-seed-entities CLI flag to opt out. The seeded set includes 4 RuView sensing-derived entities and 6 conventional HA fixtures. After a fresh restart with --db :memory:, the web UI Dashboard and States pages are fully populated on first paint.

chunks.title: Release v1404
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1404, the HOMECORE web UI gains an Add Entity flow with a modal and form. A toolbar button opens a modal containing an EntityForm with entity_id, state, and attributes fields. Client-side validation checks entity_id format, non-empty state, and JSON object attributes. On successful creation, the modal closes, a toast confirms, and the dashboard refreshes.

chunks.title: Release v1405
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1405, the HOMECORE web UI adds an Edit Entity modal. Clicking a state card on the Dashboard opens the modal in edit mode with pre-populated fields and a locked entity_id. The card is made focusable with shadow-DOM focus delegation. The modal heading and primary button text change based on mode, and the submit toast reflects whether the entity was created or updated.

chunks.title: Release v1406
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1406, the HOMECORE web UI implements entity deletion. The backend adds a DELETE /api/states/<id> handler that returns 204 No Content idempotently. The frontend adds a delete button on state cards that appears on hover/focus, a confirmation modal naming the entity, and a toast on successful deletion. The card's click-to-edit handler is prevented from firing when the delete button is clicked.

chunks.title: Release v1407
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1407, the HOMECORE web UI adds live per-field validation and inline server error display. The EntityForm shows validity feedback on every keystroke with green checkmarks, red errors, or amber warnings. A warning is shown for unknown entity domains. Server-side rejection text is surfaced inline in the form's error block instead of the page top.

chunks.title: Release v1408
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1408, the HOMECORE web UI Services page adds a Call Service feature. Each service pill has a Call button that opens a modal with a JSON textarea for service_data, live JSON validation, and a response block. The modal displays the target URL, and the Call button is disabled on invalid JSON or while a request is pending. A toast confirms the call result.

chunks.title: Release v1409
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1409, the HOMECORE web UI Settings page adds probe-before-persist token validation. The bearer-token editor probes /api/config with the new value before writing to localStorage, preventing lock-out from a typo'd or revoked token. Three actions are provided: Test token, Probe & Save, and Clear. Inline probe results show acceptance, latency, and server version, or an error message.

chunks.title: Release v1421
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1421, the frontend directory is moved to examples/frontend/, reflecting that the Lit + Vite HOMECORE web UI is an example consumer of the sensing stack rather than a top-level deliverable. An entry is added to examples/README.md for discoverability.

chunks.title: Release v1428
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1428, ADR-134 is implemented to add first-class Channel Impulse Response estimation in the Rust workspace. The algorithm uses ISTA L1 sparse recovery with a Tikhonov-regularised warm start via NeumannSolver. Performance measurements are provided for HT20, HE20, HT40, and HE40 tiers. A cross-platform deterministic witness is established using a quantised-magnitude profile in natural index order.

chunks.title: RuView Streaming Engine v0.3.0 — Auditable Environmental Intelligence
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v0.3.0-streaming-engine, the RuView Streaming Engine is introduced with a focus on auditable environmental intelligence. It includes a WorldGraph for typed digital twin representation and trusted semantic records with evidence trails. New capabilities span frame contracts, calibration, fusion quality, array coordination, privacy control, evolution detection, RF-SLAM, UWB fusion, an ablation harness, and an RF encoder. The engine composition root runs the full trust pipeline in one process_cycle().

chunks.title: Release v1444
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1444, ADR-147 integrates the OccWorld world model via a new wifi-densepose-worldmodel v0.3.0 crate. It provides an async Unix-socket bridge to an OccWorld Python inference server, occupancy grid encoding, and trajectory prior injection into the pose tracker. Benchmark proof shows 208.7 ms P50 inference and 3.37 GB peak VRAM on an RTX 5080.

chunks.title: Release v1447
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1447, a fix is applied to use the published worldgraph v0.3.0 crate instead of a path dependency, in preparation for publishing to crates.io.

chunks.title: Release v1448
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1448, ADR-147 Phase 3 and 5 are implemented, adding a RuViewOccDataset domain adapter that converts WorldGraph JSON snapshots to OccWorld tensors with indoor class remapping, and a retraining pipeline with scripts for recording snapshots, fine-tuning the VQVAE tokenizer, and fine-tuning the autoregressive transformer. The wifi-densepose-worldmodel v0.3.0 crate is published to crates.io.

chunks.title: Release v1449
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1449, documentation is updated to add the Phase 3 and 5 scripts to the user guide and README world model row, describing the full retrain workflow and noting the fine-tune capability.

chunks.title: Release v1450
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1450, real CSI benchmark results are added to the ADR-147 documentation, showing a median inference time of 208 ms, 3.98 GB VRAM usage, and 72 frames per second using the v1 CSI proof dataset.

chunks.title: Release v1451
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1451, ADR-147 Phase 4 and 6 deliver a Candle Rust port of the OccWorld model with VQVAE and transformer components, and GCP GPU scripts for provisioning and running training on A100 GPUs. The Candle port includes 14 passing tests and supports dummy and loaded inference.

chunks.title: Release v1484
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1484, a new ruview-swarm crate is added implementing ADR-148 drone swarm control with hierarchical-mesh topology, Raft consensus, MAPPO MARL, CSI sensing integration, and ITAR-gated coordination features. It includes modules for types, topology, formation, planning, allocation, sensing, MARL, security, failsafe, configuration, demo, integration, and orchestration. Benchmark results show MARL actor inference at 3.3 µs, RRT-APF planning at 0.043 ms, and 3-view localization accuracy of 1.732 m. The crate is later renamed from wifi-densepose-swarm to ruview-swarm, and Ruflo AI-agent capabilities are integrated behind a feature gate.

chunks.title: Release v1506
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1506, ADR-149 adds an evaluation harness for the swarm system, including GDOP calculation, IQM with bootstrap confidence intervals, and a noise sweep kinematic evaluator. The harness produces a leaderboard in RESULTS.md, comparing coverage and localization precision across strategies.

chunks.title: Release v1528
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1528, a pull request merges the ADR-149 Aether Arena spatial-intelligence benchmark, adding a scorer and CI harness gate.

chunks.title: Release v1544
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1544, a fix pins the determinism lock to numpy 2.4.2 to match the published hash, ensuring proof reproducibility.

chunks.title: Release v1548
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1548, a firmware fix addresses the capture of DATA frames on display-less boards, resolving the root cause of zero packets per second yield.

chunks.title: Release v1551
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1551, an MQTT fix ensures one Home-Assistant device per node, closing issue #898.

chunks.title: Release v1553
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1553, an occupancy fix bounds the eigenvalue person-count to the single-link maximum, addressing issue #894.

chunks.title: Release v1555
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1555, the firmware release bins are refreshed with the CSI fix from issue #893, resulting in version v0.6.7.

chunks.title: Release v1557
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1557, a fix passes the required configuration to the DensePoseHead in the v1 API, restoring a green main CI.

chunks.title: Release v1560
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the ruvnet/RuView release v1560, a CI fix adds MOCK_POSE_DATA and declares psutil for the v1 API, resulting in green Performance Tests and API Docs.

prototypes.window_summary: This window tracks the recent seaweedfs/seaweedfs release stream from version 3.98 through 4.31, covering major architectural changes, S3 API enhancements, erasure coding improvements, and new features like the weed mini command and Iceberg catalog support.

chunks.memory_unit_text: In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 3.98, the release includes Helm chart fixes for volume annotations and global repository values, a master change to add a disable volume_growth flag, volume server improvements to create new volumes on less occupied disk locations, message queue additions including SQL querying and a Kafka gateway, S3 API fixes for signature verification and error responses, and FUSE mount enhancements for disk cache validation and memory leak fixes.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 3.99, the release includes filer metadata subscription optimization to avoid repeated disk reads, S3 API fixes for SSE-S3 key manager concurrent writes and decryption, a requirement for JWT tokens on all volume server read operations, shell improvements for command history and a helper function, worker refactoring using command-query pattern, and admin UI login fix for securecookie errors.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.00, the release includes S3 API additions for advanced IAM config file support, CORS fallback, and auth with X-Forwarded headers, filer fixes for Azure SDK migration bugs and retry mechanism for failed deletions, Docker container non-root user support, Helm chart PVC template compatibility, master vacuum fix and faster startup with peers=none option, and erasure coding refactoring.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.01, a major architectural change introduces direct S3 API to volume server access, bypassing the filer for data operations, reducing write latency by 30% and read latency by 5%. The release also includes S3 enhancements for bucket policy enforcement, JWT generation for volume server auth, and support for multiple filers with automatic failover, along with metrics for concurrent upload tracking.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.02, the release includes master fix for too many pings and EC shard evacuation safety check, volume server improvements for disk check random source selection and separate vacuum speed, filer additions for Redis username and keyPrefix support and async empty folder cleanup, S3 API fixes for SSE-S3 copy, chunked encoding, and multipart uploads with more than 1000 parts, and FUSE mount read throughput improvement with parallel chunk fetching.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.03, the release adds TUS protocol support for resumable HTTP uploads in the filer and merges the IAM server into the S3 server. It includes S3 fixes for versioning listing bugs, presigned POST uploads, and CORS wildcard matching, filer fixes for webhook duplicate deliveries and memory allocation reductions, volume server fixes for mount restoration and needle read panics, and filer backup and sync improvements for batching and checkpoint saving.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.04, the release introduces the 'weed mini' command for beginners and test/dev environments, which automatically starts all core components. It includes shell humanized output for weed.server, S3 API fixes for ETag format, memory leaks in ListObjectVersions, and bucket size/object count metrics, and various other fixes for EC rebalance, remote storage caching, and bucket listing permissions.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.05, the release includes admin and worker fixes for file browser URL handling and Kubernetes health checks, Helm chart support for volume server ID and multiple S3 ingress hosts, S3 API additions for volume encryption, SOSAPI support for Veeam integration, and service account support, along with fixes for authorization bypass and object tagging in versioned buckets.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.06, the release includes Helm chart fixes for admin metrics port and filer template volume mount, S3 API fixes for list objects marker adjustment, directory listing, and STS credential signature, support for AWS standard IAM role ARN formats, and storage class in extended attributes, filer fixes for GCS credential conflict and JWT error, and FUSE mount writeback_cache and async_dio options.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.07, the release includes Helm chart fixes for extraEnvironmentVars and filer fallback, admin UI fixes for master server display and bucket permission persistence, S3 API additions for AssumeRole and AssumeRoleWithLDAPIdentity STS actions, S3 policy variables, and wildcard matching correction, volume server bootstrap persistent state and compact map race fix, and master split-brain prevention with persistent ClusterID and join validation.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.09, the release includes S3 API fixes for CopyObject If-Match ETag, OIDC claims propagation, CORS headers for non-existent buckets, and conditional writes with versioning, IAM storage refactoring to multi-file backend, IAM policy management via gRPC, and the introduction of S3 Tables support for Iceberg tabular data with an Iceberg REST Catalog server and admin UI.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.12, the release includes admin UI fixes for maintenance task sorting and capacity leak, filer command panic fix, Helm chart additions for Iceberg REST catalog ingress and S3 service traffic distribution, S3 API fixes for ListObjectVersions delimiter inconsistency, multipart upload ETag calculation, and health check endpoints, and erasure coding enhancements with volume.scrub and ec.scrub commands, index scrubbing, and parallelization.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.13, the release includes S3 Table Bucket and Iceberg Catalog support for multi-level namespaces, pagination, namespace properties, and commit reliability, S3 API fixes for ListObjectsV2 NextContinuationToken, lifecycle TTL rules, and IAM identity loss on restart, filer sync support for manifest chunks, and shell command volumeServer.state to query/update volume server state settings.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.15, a major change auto-migrates maintenance scripts to an Admin Script worker managed by the Admin Server, introducing a new plugin system for workers. The release includes admin UI and worker refactoring, S3 API additions for md5 checksum validation, managed policy storage, and IAM group management, and volume server EC fallback for missing ecx files.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.16, the release includes Helm chart updates for OpenShift support and custom S3 HTTPS certificate, admin UI and worker improvements for job type categories, batch volume balance, and paginated bucket listing, S3 API IAM policy fallback authorization and group management, S3 Table Bucket iceberg_maintenance plugin worker, and FUSE mount metadata cache rebuild snapshot consistency.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.17, the release includes admin UI and worker fixes for nil pointer crash during vacuum compaction, dynamic timeouts for plugin worker vacuum gRPC calls, and sidebar menu cleanup, S3 API persistence of bucket counter metrics across idle periods, and fixes for trust policy validation and ListObjects with trailing-slash prefix.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.18, the release includes Helm chart fixes for topology spread constraints, service name truncation, and all-in-one maxVolumes, miscellaneous improvements for log rotation with gzip compression and JSON structured logging, Kafka gateway response deadlock fixes, and TUS chunked upload and resume failure fixes.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.19, the release includes S3 API additions for STS GetCallerIdentity and GetFederationToken, concurrent chunk prefetch for large file downloads, and canned ACL to file permissions mapping, admin UI and worker fixes for urlPrefix and profiling options, and filer sync active chunk transfer display.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.20, the release includes S3 API and IAM additions for ListUserPolicies and group inline policy actions, FUSE mount distributed lock cross-mount write coordination and POSIX compliance improvements, master size-aware volume assignment with weighted selection, and Helm chart documentation for worker job categories.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.21, the release announces 100% POSIX compliance for FUSE Mount, peer-to-peer file chunk sharing, optimization for all-to-all parallel downloading for AI use cases, and a new NFS server. It includes S3 API performance improvements for large file reads with shared in-memory chunk cache, and FUSE mount write buffer cap and proactive flush of idle writable chunks.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.22, the release includes shell fixes for volume.fsck broken chunk manifest handling and ec.encode health-check key mismatch, mount fixes for non-UTF-8 filenames and dirty handle flushing, filer performance parallelization of StreamMutateEntry, and master topology drop of per-disk task-type conflict map.

chunks.title: 4.23 (Not safe for erasure coding and multi-disk volume servers)
chunks.memory_unit_text: In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.23, noted as not safe for erasure coding and multi-disk volume servers, the release includes shell fixes for volume.list writable filter and volume.balance exact match filter, S3 API fixes for remote object caching, cross-SSE copy operations, and IAM user creation performance, and filer sync addition of -verifySync mode for cross-cluster file comparison.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.24, the release includes volume server fixes for EC shard loading on multi-disk servers, balance not moving remote-tiered volumes, and authentication on destructive gRPC admin endpoints, S3 Table Bucket and Iceberg Catalog integration tests with Apache Doris and Unity Catalog, and miscellaneous pruning of unused functions.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.25, a quick follow-up to 4.24, the release includes admin UI fix for attaching admin-signed Bearer token on filer IAM gRPC calls, erasure coding fix for clearing cross-server stale EC shards before re-distribution, and Docker image CI tagging of latest in unified release.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.26, the release includes erasure coding distributed EC read across peer servers and mirroring of EC sidecars onto every shard-bearing disk, mini command quieter startup with progress board, Helm chart decoupling of JWT signing from cert-manager mTLS, and S3 API fix for ListBucketsHandler with pathStyleDomains.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.27, the release includes FUSE mount fix for not releasing file handles from FUSE Forget, S3 API support for group inline policies and bucket configuration handlers, volume server acceptance of legacy needle CRC encoding, and admin server file browser upload/download switch to filer gRPC.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.28, the release includes S3 API fixes for audit log requester population, server-side copy data collection, and empty directory listing, volume server EC shard packing onto fewer disks, filer sync offset freshness, and master acceptance of volume-server Ping targets on follower masters.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.29, the release includes admin server and worker EC placement shared replica-placement resolver and Prometheus metrics exposure, S3 API routing of object writes off the distributed lock using ObjectTransaction, and FUSE mount POSIX advisory lock set primitive for distributed locking.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.30, the release includes S3 API fixes for metadata spec compliance in Iceberg, MetadataDirective REPLACE on CopyObject, and anonymous unsigned-streaming PutObject, filer removal of the inode-to-path index and NFS gateway, master timeout on AllocateVolume/DeleteVolume, and volume server EC bitrot detection with per-shard checksum sidecars.

In the seaweedfs/seaweedfs release 4.31, the release includes S3 API short-circuit filer failover on ErrNotFound, versioned PutObject transaction commit, and multipart upload ETag compatibility with Hadoop S3A, admin server file browser inline image/PDF viewing and metadata export, volume server maxVolumeCount dead zone fix and EC bitrot detection follow-ups, and Terraform support for VM-based deployment.
